as we have heard, this is an important own-initiative report and an important subject. it affects not just many, but many, many workers. about 4 million people have been affected in the last 10 years, with around 14 000 to 15 000 company transformations. but it's also important to note that these transformations are very different. from outsourcing to relocation, from internal restructuring to relocation, from reorganisation of forms of activity, there is a lot of stuff, and there are a lot of rules. we've heard a lot of people talk about it, but that doesn't necessarily mean that we need to standardize the rules. two conflicting demands are presented. from the point of view of the workers, there is clearly a need for greater stability, for better foresight and for more planning. a legitimate claim, and where possible, it should be created, and the parties involved should cooperate in this. on the other hand, we're in the middle of a crisis. to be competitive, businesses must adapt quickly to changing conditions, transform, reorganise if you will. to do this, they need more flexibility. i think that it would be very difficult to have regulation at european level to deal with this, and it has no legal basis at the moment, because the treaty assigns the regulation of labour law, labour law, to the competence of the nations. it is an old debate whether a single european labour law system would be a good thing in a single market. i think it's probably true, but there's no way to do that right now. i therefore agree with what the commission has proposed: to take account of good practice, to help, to bring the social partners together and to learn from each other, but i think that a single directive is too much. i'm glad we were able to compromise with the reporter. some kind of act is acceptable, no directive is needed.
it is very important to pay special attention to disabled employees during restructuring. and the training that they're getting in the transition should be accessible, accessible, otherwise they're going to be among the first to be laid off because of the lack of it. few people know that for older and disabled workers, the cost of training them in small and medium-sized enterprises is a worthwhile investment. in countries where the job crisis is not so severe, it might be worth paying attention to this, because who are the first to be fired? disabled workers. the requirement to prevent redundancies due to restructuring is acceptable as a transitional solution, but cannot be a general prescription. care must be taken that redundancies do not lead to more and more redundancies because the financial situation of enterprises is deteriorating. so what do we do? local labour market services need to be strengthened and i would like to draw particular attention to the fact that, in the midst of low levels of training, the european union has no strategy for training. i ask that the european commission develops a strategy for the low-skilled as soon as possible.

in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. it would, for example, include a ban on uninitiated sovereign ratings and examine whether a credit rating agency can even rate a member state's creditworthiness. the adoption of the draft law may further restrict the merger of credit rating agencies that have already generated significant income from rating activities, as well as the previously unlimited ratings of structured finance products. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − the european union is regulating the market for the third time in less than three years, from the first round of mandatory registration and the placing of credit rating agencies under the direct control of the european supervisory authority to the current comprehensive regulation, which is expected to pave the way for profound changes in the sector. one of the main anomalies is the excessive reliance on the opinions of credit rating agencies. european and national legislation currently confers institutional status on credit ratings in many cases, for example, the capital requirements for banks are not linked to credit rating opinions in one country alone. this was a very bad direction, and in my view it raises a number of problems. i voted in favour of the report as it obliges financial institutions to strengthen their own credit risk analysis and not rely solely and mechanically on external credit ratings.
in writing. − it is unacceptable that global economic developments and the assessment of individual countries' economies are influenced by credit ratings which, in recent years, have been responsible for deepening the economic crisis through a series of faulty and sometimes self-serving ratings. unfounded and unjustified downgrades increase financial market uncertainty and could push already struggling european states into further recession. the report adopted today allows for a review of shareholding in multiple credit rating agencies and introduces rotation in case of multiple ratings, which increases competition between credit rating agencies. i am voting in favour of not only making us the victims of unfounded ratings, but also of having a proper regulatory framework to ensure the transparent operation of credit rating agencies and to prevent unfounded ratings in the future.
in writing. − the widespread incorporation of credit ratings into legal instruments such as the ucits and aif directives may influence the use of credit ratings by regulated entities, the basis on which the managers of those entities decide in favour of the institutions concerned, and the competition between the institutions. it should be borne in mind that credit ratings are merely opinions on the future relative credit risk of legal entities, credit obligations or debt and equity securities and are useful measures of future creditworthiness. they do not measure other risks and therefore cannot be used as a tool to assess other characteristics of the securities in which ucits and aifs invest, such as liquidity risks, price volatility or marketability. i voted in favour of mr domenici's report, because i too can only support the legislative proposal put forward by the european commission. in my view, the general principle of avoiding excessive reliance on external credit ratings should be incorporated into the risk management procedures and systems of ucits and aifm managers and adapted to their specificities. i therefore believe that in the medium term further initiatives should be assessed, also for the reason that the rating should not be included in financial regulation.
in writing. − under the rules of procedure, if the number of candidates for the election of vice-presidents is equal to the number of vacancies, the president may order the candidates to be elected by a public call or by secret ballot. in the case of a public vote, the president shall decide at the same time on the rank of the vice-presidents. in practice, however, the election of vice-presidents is carried out by a public ballot, where there is agreement between the political groups on the persons to be appointed. the ranking of the vice-presidents shall then be determined by secret ballot. this solution is based on the fact that, although the groups usually agree on the persons to be elected, they do not agree on their place in the hierarchy, so that there would be no consensus on the decision of the president. in such cases, the president shall not exercise the prerogative of deciding on the ranking of the vice-presidents, which is provided for in parliament's rules of procedure. the purpose of this draft report is to amend the rules of procedure of the european parliament in order to bring it into line with parliament's practice.

next item declaration by the vice-president of the commission / high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the recommendations of the review conference of the npt on the establishment of a middle east free of weapons of mass destruction
in writing. the draft resolution of the review conference of the npt on the middle east free of weapons of mass destruction confronts european decision-makers with the major security challenges of our time. the question of action on iran's nuclear programme, as is well known, presents the entire transatlantic alliance with serious dilemmas. the overall security situation is further aggravated by the presence of a stockpile of highly dangerous chemical weapons in the hands of the syrian government, which, given the ongoing civil war in syria, could at any time spiral out of control. the road to a world free of weapons of mass destruction is a long and winding one. but we must not give up on the goal. at the same time, a world free of weapons of mass destruction cannot be achieved unilaterally, only on the basis of a treaty reflecting the common will and action of all parties concerned. of course, the civil use of nuclear energy may still be needed, but it is essential from a safety point of view to eliminate the risks of dual use. the european union will play a key role in creating a world free of weapons of mass destruction and, in particular, the nuclear threat. that is why i support this resolution.

my fellow citizens! this is a very important issue, as millions of passengers face the problem of conflicting information on their baggage on the airline website and, in some cases, oversized or overweight baggage at the airport. in such cases, airlines charge a disproportionate surcharge and often put passengers in a humiliating position. passenger rights are often violated, and this needs to be addressed as soon as possible. a general solution needs to be worked out. the european parliament has already dealt with this issue on several occasions, but i myself believe that a single charter of passenger rights is needed to deal with this issue. i've had speakers before me talk about musicians, women's handbags, and i'd like to talk about disability issues. we cannot allow any arbitrary regulations on the taking on board of the equipment, medical aids and medicines necessary for their independent life, because we are talking about the rights of citizens.
to what extent do the 1 hand baggage rule introduced by each airline take into account the interests of passengers? how much does it restrict passenger rights? the current practice is not harmonised, there are no uniform standards, so passengers have to compare prices and other conditions when buying air tickets, which is admittedly not an easy task. the regulations introduced by discount airlines a few years ago are causing increasing problems for passengers, as they are difficult to follow and compare with the practices of other airlines, not to mention that exceeding the limit is punished by a heavy surcharge, which can be several times the ticket price. the introduction of a uniform regime cannot therefore be delayed any longer in order to protect passengers and preserve the viability of the retail establishments operating at the airport. the european parliament has already addressed this issue in several resolutions. on 23 october 2012, it adopted an own-initiative report calling on the european commission to finally regulate the carriage of hand luggage on machinery. that's what you should do.
in writing . european citizens are almost completely exposed to the almost constantly changing baggage rules of mostly budget airlines. passengers often find conflicting information on the airline's website about baggage that can be taken on board and in many cases only at the airport do they find that their baggage is oversized or overweight, as per the individual regulations of the airlines. the airlines, especially the low-cost airlines, can also, in my view, impose disproportionate surcharges because of the excess weight and the larger size. this inappropriate behaviour must, in my opinion, be stopped immediately. i think the commission should take the necessary steps, because we need new regulations, a kind of unification. i myself have witnessed on many occasions during my travels that passengers have been humiliated when checking the size of their bags and in many cases have been forced to choose between paying the surcharge or throwing out certain items. i believe that in these cases the rights of passengers can be fundamentally violated. this is why it is necessary to restrict this behaviour of airlines as soon as possible and to bring it under uniform regulation. i therefore welcome the tran committee's proposal and can only hope that we will be able to discuss this matter under an accelerated procedure.

as a result of the reparations following the change of regime, two million hungarian people got back their rightful property, their land, which was taken away during the communist era. although the form of compensation had a disastrous effect on agriculture, its social justice and moral basis are still unquestioned. in contrast, the current hungarian government's new land law project threatens their property. the new regulations will narrow down the range of buyers, lower the price of land. this will drastically devalue the wealth of 1.5 million hungarian people. many, not just the owners, thought that by selling a few acres of their land, they could afford to send their children and grandchildren to school, to buy a home, or to supplement their pension. we cannot allow the orbán government to seriously harm one and a half million people. it cannot be allowed to infringe eu fundamental law by restricting the right to private property.
in writing. the new common fisheries policy should pay greater attention to aquaculture, including freshwater fisheries. marine fisheries are unsustainable: 30% of the world's seas are overfished, meaning that there are not enough fish left to sustain the population. according to the un food and agriculture organization, this has already led to a significant decline in catches of 2% in 2012. aquaculture, on the other hand, ensures sustainable fish production. freshwater fish farming, for which hungary has excellent potential, not only contributes to food security but can also create a significant number of jobs and help maintain biodiversity, as freshwater lakes, as aquatic habitats, provide habitat for numerous bird and other animal species, most of which are under natura 2000 protection. the financial support for the aquaculture sector from the eu budget should therefore be significantly increased in the 2014-2020 budget period.

in writing. − the process of globalisation as such and civil society require companies to behave more responsibly. proper communication and joint action between the company, its partners and wider society make it possible to strengthen an enterprise and, indirectly, its competitiveness. improving transparency, self- and co-regulation processes in addition to sectoral regulation will contribute to the achievement of the general objectives of csr. the spectacular reduction of the gap between citizens and businesses increases citizens' trust in businesses, which is necessary for a sustainable economic recovery. smes can play a key role in corporate social responsibility, as they are the backbone of the union's economy. through smes, csr can spread much faster and smes in the same sector have the opportunity to tackle similar social and environmental problems together.
in writing. − research shows that social enterprises may significantly contribute to the fulfilment of the europe 2020 objectives. therefore the twofold goal set forth in the commission’s communication, and also in this report, to recognise already existing social businesses and to pave the way for the creation of new and innovative forms needs to be pursued and more effectively communicated. the commission should create an online public database of fair businesses, quality schemes and labels to serve as a multilingual information and exchange platform for social entrepreneurs, business and social investors, and also to facilitate accessibility to csr information and improve transparency. a european regulatory framework for ethical investment funds and a quantified headline target on social businesses also need to be developed by the commission in cooperation with the member states, in order to support social businesses through eu policies, and to increase their number and consequently the jobs they create.
in writing. − the current economic crisis has been driven by a lack of transparency, accountability and corporate responsibility, and short-term thinking. we must learn from this. we do not want to live in a europe that is controlled only by the banks. companies need to be aware of the impact they have on society. i believe that if all companies exercise their social responsibility correctly, it can go a long way towards regaining the lost public trust. this is essential for sustainable economic growth and to mitigate the social impact of the crisis. it is also necessary to define specific measures within the framework of corporate social responsibility aimed at combating misleading and false information about the environmental and social impacts of products and services. we cannot allow the fraudulent practices that deceive consumers, authorities and investors to further erode trust in companies.
in writing. − the eu's csr policy should be implemented in a way that complements national legislation. however, i do not support universal solutions which do not take into account the specificities of the national markets and sectors in which companies operate and which may, where appropriate, lead to an increase in administrative burdens. appropriate flexibility should therefore be ensured in the implementation of the csr guidelines in order to adapt to the specific requirements of each member state and region, in particular as regards the capacities of smes. the responsibility of enterprises for their impact on society is to strive to produce the greatest possible shared value for their owners and other stakeholders, and for society at large. this makes it possible to identify and prevent possible negative effects arising in the course of the company's operations.
in writing. − the eu economy is going through its most difficult period since its creation, and effective taxation is now a particularly important element in the attempt to consolidate member states' public finances rapidly. vat fraud is a highly damaging practice that reduces member states' budget revenues by a significant amount and thus hinders their efforts to consolidate public finances. the various forms of vat fraud are changing relatively quickly and therefore the regulation aimed at eliminating such activity should be designed in the most effective way possible. i voted in favour of this report because, by introducing a rapid reaction mechanism, the proposed directive will significantly reduce the time needed to approve special measures to combat tax fraud and evasion and this amendment could increase the likelihood that such cases will be dealt with more effectively.

in writing. to keep energy prices under control, the unimpeded flow of energy must be ensured. while energy infrastructure is developed in western europe, there is still a lack of physical connectivity between central and eastern european countries, which means that the single market is not functioning. this is why our region's energy markets are characterised by unilateral energy dependence and high energy prices. the european commission intends to encourage the development of the missing networks in the future. to this end, it declares the investment of major importance to be of public interest, which confers important advantages on the investors. the timeframe for approving public investments is drastically reduced to three and a half years. this is a major improvement over the previous practice, which often took ten years to obtain permits. the advantage of preferential status is also that it allows for cheaper financing. since the public-sector developments also met the european commission's strict evaluation criteria, they also represent a lower risk for the creditors than an average investment. investments that are important for security of supply but not economically viable may be supported by direct union financial resources. this could also lead to strategic investments to ensure uninterrupted energy supply in a crisis situation. i hope that today's package of measures will finally break the deadlock and rebuild the missing infrastructure. as investment in central and eastern europe has a good chance of qualifying for preferential status, i see a chance for the first time in 60 years to reduce the unilateral energy dependence of our region.

in writing. on the second anniversary of the fukushima nuclear disaster, calls for the decommissioning of nuclear power plants are again being heard. in this context, it is necessary to emphasise again and again certain ambitions of the energy roadmap 2050, which, although an extremely important document and an excellent summary of the current situation, has little basis in reality for some of its objectives. the transition to 100% renewable energy by 2050 is in principle a worthwhile endeavour, but in practice some member states, such as hungary, are unable to achieve this due to their geographical location, let alone financial constraints. as a consequence, if nuclear energy is phased out by 2050, hungary, along with several other member states, will not be able to meet its energy needs on its own. despite the disaster that occurred two years ago, we must remain objective about nuclear energy and support the search for a more controlled and safer system rather than a mindless dismantling. the industry in the developed world is beset by ongoing financial scandals, a trend that the hungarian government may follow by completely obscuring the details of the current paks nuclear power plant expansion from the government, thus making the whole process a high risk of corruption. in summary, the european energy roadmap 2050 must be designed in the spirit of having a number of member states that rely on nuclear energy.
in writing. reducing europe's energy dependence, reducing co2 emissions and ensuring the security of energy supply are all objectives to be achieved. in addition, widespread access to cheap, yet environmentally friendly and easily manageable energy is particularly important for the population. and renewable if you can. these requirements seem to contradict each other, but if we are willing to think outside the box and learn from the more intelligent, truly progressive parts of the world, such as the brics countries, then we have a solution. this is a breeder reactor, a fourth-generation nuclear power plant, which produces additional fissile material from the normal, large quantities of the cheaply available uranium-238 isotope. it therefore meets all the criteria at once. but thorium is a cheap and abundant fissile material. only these two technologies, with the knowledge and the inventory we have today, can guarantee the entire energy supply of the earth with cheap electricity for the next 150 to 200 years. with such a prospect, is it worth it to install huge propellers on the sea, on our fallow fields, making nature ugly? do you want my uncertain, cyclical, and expensive electricity? it makes as much sense as using a silver coffee spoon to carry water from the kitchen to the garden to water the vegetables instead of using the garden tap and the sprinkler. and what my electricity won't do is clean burning natural gas. if we don't waste the gas to generate electricity, it's enough for 150 to 200 years. all other solutions are only appropriate in very extreme, hard-to-reach places. or if it is competitive on a market basis with the energy production methods proposed above. taxpayers' money is not to be wasted on useless things!
in writing. we socialists are primarily in favour of energy-saving solutions, including the insulation of family homes and the energy upgrading of apartment buildings. investing in energy efficiency can reduce household recession bills in the long run. the hungarian government's 10% reduction in the national income tax is a pittance, but it deserves support because it temporarily helps a section of the citizens: those who still have the means to pay their national income tax. it is questionable whether it will bring any relief to those most in need. instead, we need investments that keep our energy bills down, that guarantee the security of our energy supply. these include insulation of panel houses and other buildings and the development of renewable energy sources. a step is being taken across europe to introduce a general public service minimum. this would also be necessary in hungary, because this would ensure the necessary amount of electricity and gas to the citizens. this would avoid the clock being switched off for low-income consumers. it is particularly important that the european parliament pays particular attention to the social impact of energy prices and the problems of vulnerable households. more than 260 000 energy-efficient renovations of panel housing have been carried out in hungary under the panel programme launched by socialist governments. the complex energy renovation was financed by eu recovery funds, state aid and the residents' own contributions. it is unclear why the hungarian government has terminated the previously successful panel program. it has deprived hundreds of thousands of families of saving as much as 45 to 60 percent of their monthly rental bill by renovating their homes. this is the long-term solution!
the comprehensive risk and safety assessment of nuclear power plants in the european union has been successfully completed. the resilience tests were primarily aimed at assessing the reliability and preparedness of nuclear power plants. we know that the operational safety of power plants is still controlled by multi-level inspections. this control is carried out primarily by the national authorities of the member states and is carried out with the utmost thoroughness. in hungary, the national atomic energy office maintains an office in the paksi nuclear power plant site, where it constantly monitors the operation of the units, and even in the office's headquarters, they can see online all the data they need to see about the operation of the reactors and the plant. in addition, euratom and the international atomic energy agency are carrying out audits and coordinating their work. the stress test identified these mechanisms and the results confirmed that national authorities are doing an excellent job under the current system. it was a great pleasure for me that hungary, the hungarian power plant, was among the safest plants. i welcome the european council's proposal to adopt the nuclear safety directive this year, rather than wait until 2014. however, i would be wary of creating a new european level of supervision, because experience has shown that national authorities work well.

in writing. − having participated in the debate on the report and voted for it in the committee on energy, i agree with its reasoning that a sustainable, secure, uninterrupted and affordable energy supply is one of the major challenges that unites europeans, from civil society to decision-makers, industry and environmentalists. although the commission has set ambitious energy policy objectives on competitiveness, security of supply, sustainability and decarbonisation, the internal energy market is characterised by insufficient integration, a high degree of energy isolation in certain geographical areas, inadequate access to diversified energy sources that contribute to energy security, and a lack of tangible benefits for consumers and businesses in terms of prices and sustainability. this general situation and the considerable interdependence of the member states require a european approach. faster, more decisive and more coordinated action is needed.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report, as the trilogues reached a compromise acceptable from the point of view of hungarian interests. however, i still consider it unnecessary to make any specific reference to the so-called rio markers in the text. the problem is that the use of these indicators can be misleading. for example, one eu research project based on the rio benchmarks showed that hungary's exposure to climate change is not too high and therefore there is no real need for further measures. the reality, however, is that several regions in my country are increasingly vulnerable to climate change and that significant structural transformation is needed to overcome the disadvantages. as the indicator thus has a significant financial dimension, it is important to continue to address this issue.
in writing. − this legislation is a milestone in the history of european consumer protection. the range of those affected by the legislation is extremely wide, with an average of 20% of consumers in the union encountering a problem when shopping online. the new system is simple and inexpensive, as consumers have a means of redress that avoids expensive and cumbersome court proceedings. the interactive website now available will be easily accessible to the masses of shoppers with just a few clicks, and in their own language. the platform shall enable the customer with a complaint and the trader concerned to settle their dispute online through a jointly selected alternative dispute resolution body. the new system is fast, as the procedural time limit is reduced from 450 days to 90 days, as was the case in the past with the european practice. i voted in favour of the adoption of the draft law in accordance with the above.
in writing. − i welcome the european online dispute resolution platform (ovr-platform) and the directive on the alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes (avr directive), which would create an interactive website for the out-of-court settlement of contractual disputes arising in connection with the crossborder online sale of goods or services between a trader established in one member state and a consumer with a permanent residence in another member state. the interactive website would be available in all the eu's official languages, free of charge. for the purpose of out-of-court settlement, all consumer and trader complaints (e.g. non-payment or refusal to take delivery of goods) would be referred to an alternative dispute resolution body (e.g. arbitrator, conciliator, ombudsman or appeal board). the odr platform identifies the subject matter of the dispute and provides the parties with the relevant adr entities covered by the avr directive and provides the parties with the basic information (tariffs, languages, binding or non-binding legal effect of the outcome of the procedure, etc.). the parties shall then choose by agreement an adr entity that will attempt to resolve the dispute within 30 days, thus conducting the dispute resolution procedure via the internet, online. the interactive interface will be supported by a network of online dispute resolution experts.
in writing. − crossborder shopping gives consumers the opportunity to make the best possible deal in the eu's internal market. online shopping makes this even easier. however, sometimes problems may arise, such as problems with the products purchased or with transport. in order to avoid complicated, costly and time-consuming legal procedures, the european parliament is now making it easier for eu consumers to exercise their right to a fair trial. i believe it is very important that european consumers feel safe when they buy goods or services in the single market and do not face any additional risks. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that consumers who want to benefit from the opportunities offered by the single market should be able to rely on a number of effective and efficient means of redress.
in writing. − the creation of a european online dispute resolution (odr) platform would facilitate the effective resolution of out-of-court disputes. the odr platform would complement other adr entities and reduce the time taken to deal with complaints. however, i am convinced that the proposed system can only achieve these objectives if it is comprehensive, covers both cross-border and domestic transactions, while at the same time being simple, effective and preserves the right to a fair trial, i.e. does not deprive consumers of their right to seek legal redress.
in writing. − i welcome the alternative dispute resolution (adr) directive, which is an integral part of the european online dispute resolution (odr) platform, which would create an interactive website for the out-of-court settlement of contractual disputes arising in connection with the crossborder online sale of goods or services between a trader established in one member state and a consumer with a permanent residence in another member state. this method would be a simple, fast, efficient and low-cost dispute settlement method. it is estimated that consumers currently lose 0.4% of european gdp to such problems. in 2010, less than 5% of consumers reported to an avr organisation and only 9% of businesses reported ever using an avr. online commerce is an important pillar of eu economic activity, but most consumers and traders are afraid to make purchases online for fear of losing their legal recourse in the event of a dispute. the three main objectives of the directive are to cover the whole eu territory and to provide adequate information about the avr organisation to the target audience, and to ensure that the service itself is of a quality that meets the principles set out in the commission's recommendations.
in writing. − in disputes between businesses, banks, insurers and consumers, consumers do not necessarily have to go to court, but have the possibility to request the intervention of consumer protection centres, national bodies. this procedure is much faster than a court case and the parties are under a very strict obligation to cooperate. i am convinced that the new solutions outlined in mr grech's report will complement the help that eu citizens can already avail themselves of in resolving their disputes with traders in other member states. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal, as i believe that the procedure of the national bodies can produce results very quickly, since the ep report voted on today states that the procedure must be completed within 90 days of the opening of the consumer protection centres.
in writing. − the proposal on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes aims to create a simple, fast and low-cost dispute resolution mechanism aimed at the highest level of consumer protection in the union. our aim is to promote the proper functioning and completion of the internal market by achieving a high level of consumer protection, which is essential for economic growth and job creation. despite a number of improvements in consumer protection since the creation of the single market, there are still shortcomings that make life difficult for citizens, in particular consumers and smes. action at european level is needed to improve consumer redress and voluntary alternative dispute resolution schemes should be made available in all economic sectors.

mr president, my congratulations to the rapporteurs. they have done a wonderful job on this. now, at first sight, the redistribution of mandates should pose no problems. indeed, it should be the automatic consequence of enlargement. the eu admits a new member state and the new member state has the right to representation. in reality, as we know only too well, the process is far from trouble free. despite valiant attempts to base the redistribution of mandates on a technical or even a technocratic formula, the hard reality is that politics cannot be expelled from an issue as political as this one. crucially, no member state likes to lose mandates, so those who must will, in consequence of enlargement, do their level best to minimise their losses. then there is the question of how mandates should be distributed at all. the principle of digressive proportionality is there to ensure that small and medium-sized states are not disadvantaged, and are not under-represented politically. if they were to be so under-represented, then their voice would be even weaker than is the case, and large states need to be reminded that european integration is not a large state monopoly. if the eu is to work as an even-handed, democratic body, then the status of the smaller states as equals in terms of respect must be given cast iron safeguards. we know only too well from the history of europe what happens when large states regard smaller states as their satellites, where they are free to do as they will. the rules are there to ensure stability. the same holds true for the redistribution of mandates. there must be rules. in this instance, the logic of redistribution is that no state should lose more than one mandate and, equally, that digressive proportionality should be secured. those who seek to overturn these two fundamental principles are threatening the very bases of european integration and thereby run the risk of encouraging anti-european sentiments.

in writing. − as a result of the accession of croatia, the number of seats in the european parliament will increase from the current 754 to 766 as from july 2013, as we need to provide croatia with an additional 12 seats for the period until the end of the current term. however, the treaty on european union provides that the number of members of the european parliament shall not exceed 751 as from 2014. the number of mandates should therefore be reduced by 15. it is for parliament to solve the problem of how to fairly reduce the representation of the 27 member states below the 751 threshold in accordance with the principle of degressive proportionality. the solution proposed by parliament is that 12 member states will send one fewer member to parliament next year. hungary is also a member of this group. in my opinion, a pragmatic solution has been found, based on loss minimisation and resulting in the smallest possible reduction in the mandate for hungary. although hungary's population has fallen below the psychological threshold of 10 million according to the latest census data, our country would still be entitled to the representation of the 10-11 million member states according to the report just voted by the european parliament. the decision is a good compromise for hungary, since greece, which has a population of about one and a half million more than ours, will also have 21 seats, while sweden, with a population of nine and a half million, will have only 20 seats.

in writing. − reducing europe's energy dependence, reducing co2 emissions and ensuring the security of energy supply are all objectives to be achieved. widespread access to cheap, yet environmentally friendly and easily manageable energy is important. these requirements seem to contradict each other, but only in appearance. the solution is a fourth-generation nuclear power plant with a breeder reactor, which produces additional fissile material from the normal, cheaply available isotope uranium-238. it meets all the criteria. but thorium is a cheap and plentiful fissile material. these are the only two technologies that, based on what we know today, will guarantee the entire energy supply of the earth with cheap electricity for the next 150 to 200 years. with such a prospect, is it worth it to install huge propellers on the sea, on our fallow fields, making nature ugly? do you want my uncertain, cyclical, and expensive electricity? if we don't waste the gas to generate electricity, it's enough for 150 to 200 years.
in writing. − energy production in modern times is based on much more complex conditions than in the past. therefore, the focus should now be on energy planning and management of existing systems, thereby ensuring sustainable development. the rationalisation of natural resources is inevitable in any area of human activity. the european union currently has 47 nuclear power stations with more than 100 000 people living within a 30 km radius. the risk of nuclear accidents exists and will continue to exist, but no major accidents have occurred. the safety level of nuclear power plants in europe is generally considered to be high, but further safety standards should be maintained and improved for all european power plants. in view of the above, the eu nsas continued to conclude that the closure of nuclear power plants was not warranted. fukushima has had a major impact on public perceptions of nuclear power plants in individual member states, so it is important to carry out comprehensive risk and safety assessments of nuclear power plants and related activities (resistance testing), i.e. to inform and educate people about nuclear safety.

in writing. − the functioning of the endocrine system is crucial to the functioning of our body. our endocrine glands produce hormones that act as neurotransmitters in the central nervous system. it is essential for such vital functions as reproduction, growth, and development, as well as for the flow of energy that is essential for the functioning of the body. in endocrine regulation, the feedback principle applies, i. e. the production of the regulatory hormone increases as the level of the regulatory hormone in the body decreases. the endocrine system is extremely important, yet complex and fragile. a serious problem of our time is the harmful effect of the countless pollutants that we encounter every day. the commission should therefore develop the necessary legislative framework to take greater account of the risks posed by endocrine disrupting substances. the scope of the rules on materials that children come into contact with, such as textiles, toys, packaging materials, is particularly important, as our children are the most exposed to substances that damage the endocrine system. for these reasons in particular, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − the number of diseases stemming from disorders of human hormonal functions is increasing year by year. research consistently confirms that such malfunctions of the endocrine systems – which adversely affect the reproductive potential of the european population to a large extent – are mostly attributable to external factors. these triggers include for the most part lifestyle-related triggers, such as improper nutrition and stress, but endocrine disruptors are also to be found in everyday chemicals around us in furniture, food packaging, cosmetics or building materials. children and pregnant women are highly vulnerable to such harmful effects. the commission and the member states must – in line with eu policies on health and prevention – seek ways to restrict the use of harmful chemicals and pay special attention to reducing the exposure of children to such substances, for example by better regulating the production of toys and the construction of education facilities. furthermore, scientific research on ways to replace endocrine disruptors with health-neutral chemicals must be supported.
in writing. − in our resolution, we call on the commission to submit as soon as possible a proposal to enable insurance associations to operate at european level and across borders. the statute of european insurance associations would create a voluntary system in the form of an optional legal instrument allowing insurance associations to pursue their activities in different member states. it should be stressed that these legislative initiatives leave unchanged the various national laws in force and cannot be regarded as aiming at the approximation of the laws of the member states applicable to insurance associations.

in writing. − the supervision of financial sector institutions is undergoing a major transformation. the process is also driven by spontaneous sectoral developments and the organization of financial institutions into financial groups. the european union is moving towards more uniform regulation of the financial sector, which is also leading to a more uniform approach to supervision and an institutional framework. this was reinforced by the financial sector crisis, which also highlighted shortcomings. the need for unification is recognized by almost everyone, yet the process is constantly hampered. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that it is appropriate to achieve the harmonisation necessary and sufficient to ensure mutual recognition of authorisations and prudential supervision systems. the smooth functioning of the internal market requires not only legal regulation but also close and regular cooperation between the competent authorities of the member states and a significantly enhanced convergence of regulatory and supervisory practices.
in writing. − to overcome the economic crisis, stronger banking supervision and more prudent lending are needed than ever before. i therefore welcome the fact that euro area banks will have to meet stricter capital adequacy criteria. the transparency is greatly enhanced by the fact that banks will now have to report their annual profits and the state aid received in a country-wide breakdown. i voted in favor of the proposal that bankers' bonuses not exceed their annual salary. the current practice is unsustainable: while failing banks need state support, bankers take home multiple times their annual salary in the form of bonuses.
in writing. − the incorporation of prudential requirements into the form of regulations reinforces the direct applicability of the requirements to the member states. this ensures a level playing field by not allowing for the entry into force of different requirements in member states resulting from different transpositions of the directive. i voted in favour of the report as it ensures that all credit institutions and investment firms follow the same rules across the union, which especially in times of crisis strengthens confidence in the stability of credit institutions and investment firms.
in writing. − ground handling at eu airports. i voted against the opinion on the extension and further liberalisation of groundhandling services at eu airports. the basic idea is that, in order to increase the capacity of european airports, reduce delays and improve services for passengers, eu airports should fully ensure that both passengers and individual airlines are served as fully and efficiently as possible before and after they start operations. although i agree with the objectives outlined above, i did not vote in favour of the final adoption of the opinion, as such market liberalisation is not possible in the current economic situation. the commission notes that the airport services agreement with ryanair was signed on 20 june 2012 and that the agreement was signed on 27 june 2012.
in writing. − the aviation industry had high hopes for the european commission's proposal. in my view, the problem identified is twofold: on the one hand, ground handling is not sufficiently efficient and, on the other hand, its quality in terms of reliability, flexibility, protection, safety and environmental protection is generally not keeping pace with changing needs. although the proposal represents a significant step forward compared to the existing legislative framework, i believe that, even after the rejection last december, there were still substantive issues that would have required further discussion. i agree with the market players that the proposal may further increase the pressure on the ground handling companies. this would also lead to a fall in wage levels, a deterioration in job security and training opportunities for workers, and an increase in part-time and temporary employment. i therefore voted against the amended proposal.
in writing. − efficient ground handling is of paramount importance to passengers, airports and airlines, and i therefore agree with the introduction of standards to ensure quality of service. the full market opening proposed in the field of groundhandling services as a result of the economic crisis would not bring any tangible benefits to consumers but would further increase the burden on the undertakings providing groundhandling services. this would lead to a reduction in the wages of employees and to a deterioration in the security of employment and the training opportunities of workers. that's why i voted against the mandatory full market opening.
in writing. − ensuring equal opportunities for women and men is one of the european union's main political aspirations. one of the objectives of my colleague from gurkhas report was to assess the extent and consequences of the implementation of directive 2004/113/ec by the member states, to identify the existing shortcomings and to propose possible solutions to fill them. his suggestions are sound. i am convinced that the creation of a public database of legislation and case law relating to gender discrimination could improve the protection of victims of gender discrimination. i therefore voted in favour of the report, as i agree with the honourable member that there is a need for greater transparency in the measures taken.
in writing. − the directive implementing the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services has not yet been transposed in some member states or the legislation is too broadly formulated for implementation, while on the other hand, some countries have widened the scope to cover education too. despite some questionable issues addressed – such as how compatible the equal treatment principle’s application to media and advertising is with freedom of the press – i voted in favour of the report, because it is highly important to address the widespread discrimination of women in this field, especially in relation to the planning of childbearing, pregnancy, maternity and breastfeeding. it is to be welcomed too that the directive shifts the burden of proof so that respondents must prove the absence of breach with regard to the principle of equal treatment. the necessity of proper statistical data and reliable information is also to be emphasised, in order to enable legislators to amend the rules according to the relevant case law as well as to improve the protection of victims.
in writing. − multinational enterprises often have a significant impact on the societies and environments of developing countries and are responsible for the impact they have on local communities: they can help or hinder development. fair wages, adequate and healthy working conditions and the possibility of forming or joining a trade union are the absolute minimum requirements that european companies must meet for their employees in developing countries. i supported this report because i believe that we have a moral obligation to help reduce poverty and alleviate suffering in the world. this can be done effectively by developing trade agreements that allow developing countries to participate effectively in the international economy and to reap the benefits of globalisation.
in writing. − economic growth in developing countries has been exemplary in recent years, often in contradiction with conventional economic trends, and has consistently outpaced that of developed countries. the flow of capital, goods and labour between developing countries is now growing faster than trade between developing and developed countries. the strength of these markets also has a positive impact on the world economy, as it can partially offset the impact of the economic slowdown in the developed world. they have developed disciplined financial structures that are able to keep up with rapid market changes and attract foreign investment. in some cases, of course, the problem may be the problem of obtaining capital. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the proposals put forward by my colleague, mr saïfi, can help reduce inequalities and promote growth.

in writing. − the european ombudsman has recently taken promising steps to make his work more transparent for the citizens of the union. i think that this approach can be particularly appreciated now, in the year of the european citizen. the ombudsman places a high priority on respect for the fundamental rights of eu citizens and encourages reasoned legislation. i consider special reports by the ombudsman on priority complaints to be an exemplary practice. the intended objectives of such reports - such as enhancing transparency - are welcome, as trust in public institutions is one of the most important indicators of democracy. citizens' complaints also highlight certain weaknesses in the eu's public administration system, such as competency gaps. in high-profile cases, special reports or opinions by the ombudsman should also be encouraged in order to gain a deeper understanding of the cases and maintain the trust of the citizens.
in writing. − i would like to welcome the audit report of the european ombudsman, which confirmed that the office operates without significant budgetary shortcomings. however, there is room for improvement in its administrative functioning with regard to the increase in the length of inquiries conducted by the european ombudsman. it is highly advisable to shorten the time of procedures so that the vast majority of inquiries could be closed in no more than twelve months. it would be beneficial therefore if the ombudsman could present his own insight and suggestions in the annual report with regard to the steps that he considers necessary for enhancing the effectiveness and efficiency of the office.

in writing. − following the presentation of the annual report of the european external action service for the financial year 2011, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for the service in the context of the closure procedure for 2011. the european external action service is affected by the closure procedure for the first time, as 2011 was the institution's first full financial year, which gave particular significance to this year's discharge. the final report draws attention to the following points, among others: in 2011 a large number of new recruits were recruited at once, which was achieved by a very costly procedure of selecting 118 out of 8800 applicants. the analysis of the total cost of the recruitment process was not available to the expert committee during the final clearance procedure. as the people's party's rapporteur on the report, i also said in the plenary debate that the problem is also the real estate management of the eeas. in some cases, the cost of real estate leases is skyrocketing. the eeas explains such cases by the characteristics of the local property market, the security situation in the host country. it is particularly important to monitor the management of the service's property in the closing accounts for the coming years, as the new financial regulation allows the service to borrow and the eeas plans to purchase its own property. the issue of geographical balance is also highlighted in the report: member states that joined in 2004 and 2007 are under-represented at all levels of the organisation of the european external action service, and the vacancies should be used to strengthen the institution's geographical balance. it is particularly welcome that it has been included in the discharge report that new employees of the service must declare that they have not previously worked for a state intelligence service. in the plenary vote, i voted in favor of granting the foreign service immunity.

in writing. − the balance of payments proposal under discussion today is a welcome initiative in its essence, aimed at simplifying procedures for financial assistance between the euro area and non-euro area countries. however, amendments and additions were necessary, which were dealt with excellently by mrs hübner in her present report. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that its contents are beyond doubt. we can all see that to overcome the current problems, several building blocks are needed: such as financial stability, strengthening national responsibility, solidarity, achieving sustainable growth. if one of these elements is missing, then the problems we are discussing cannot be solved. the prior agreement will, inter alia, fundamentally increase the transparency and accountability of the procedure for applying for and awarding financial assistance to member states in difficulty and it is essential that the same transparency and accountability be increased for this proposal.
in writing. − i believe it is important that the eu financial safety net for the stability of the euro is not only for the benefit of the euro group countries but also, if necessary, for the benefit of the member states not in the euro. that is why i voted in favour of the initiative to allow member states in difficulty outside the euro area to receive assistance from eu financial resources, such as the european stability mechanism.
in writing. − following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2011, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european railway agency in the context of the closure of accounts procedure for 2011. the committee's primary task is to monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the european court of auditors concluded that it has obtained sufficient assurance from its audits that the annual accounts of the agency for the financial year 2011 are reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. at the same time, i consider it important to emphasise that certain investments had to be cancelled or postponed because of incorrect budgetary forecasts, and that parliament has on several occasions (during the discharge debates for the financial years 2008, 2009 and 2010) drawn the attention of the agency to a greater focus on addressing the problem of carrying over appropriations from one year to the next. as a result of this failure, the committee considers that such a serious breach of the principle of annual budget cannot be accepted in the future and that, therefore, the next time such and similar serious breaches occur, the exemption should be refused. notes furthermore that the agency is aware that the use of the offices in lille and valenciennes for the operation and performance of the agency's tasks reduces efficiency and generates additional costs; the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were identified during the investigation. the commission notes that the commission did not provide any information on the amount of the aid granted to the beneficiaries. i supported the granting of the discharge in the vote in committee and in the subsequent vote in plenary on 17 april.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because this new legislation could have a positive impact on businesses by eliminating double taxation and uncertainty about tax liability. there are currently no eu vat rules on vouchers, which hampers the full potential of the single market. the creation of a consistent legal framework can also help to close any loopholes that allow companies to engage in tax avoidance behaviour that exploits differences between member states.
in writing. − at present, there are no eu vat rules for transactions relating to vouchers, and in the absence of these common rules, member states have developed their own procedures. the double taxation resulting from the lack of consistency may and does hamper commercial solutions seeking to exploit the opportunities offered by the single market, and the unintended non-taxation resulting from similar reasons gives rise to abuses. the primary objective of my proposal is therefore to establish clear, harmonised eu rules on the tax treatment of vouchers. by clarifying and harmonising the eu provisions on the taxation of vouchers, this proposal will also significantly facilitate the operation of loyalty programmes and gift vouchers.
in writing. − the amendment of the common vat rules is primarily an attempt to tackle the problem of double taxation and tax evasion. it is clear that inconsistencies in the tax rules of the member states are a major obstacle to exploiting the opportunities offered by the single market. clarification and harmonisation of the union vat system for vouchers would be in the interests of both consumers and businesses. i support the proposal to provide for a single taxation system for all types of vouchers. a common european legal framework is needed to help achieve an efficient and barrier-free internal market, while fully respecting the sovereignty of the member states in tax matters.

in writing. − following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2011, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union in respect of the eniac joint undertaking in the context of the closure procedure for the financial year 2011. the committee's primary task is to monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the report reiterates its call on the joint undertaking's management to implement the transformation of the internal control and financial information systems as soon as possible, as their deficiencies are causing errors and delays in the preparation of the financial reporting. the final accounts report draws attention to the fact that the financial audit was conducted in an orderly manner and no major deficiencies were identified beyond those mentioned. the board decided to grant the discharge at its march meeting, closing the 2011 accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. − i have strongly and resolutely supported the eu's ratification of the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance, as this would speed up the enforcement of child support and other family maintenance obligations and the action and enforcement against debtors established in third countries. the report now adopted allows the deposit of the instrument approved, as is customary in the case of international conventions, until the approval decision is received from the national authorities of each member state. they expect each member state to adopt an effective and rapid procedure to enable the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance to enter into force as soon as possible.
in writing. − the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance provides european citizens with a very useful instrument to enforce their rights against non-paying debtors who reside in third countries. the 2011 accession of the european union as a legal entity to the 2007 convention will be a great step towards the realisation of cross-border child support obligations, but an instrument of approval must be deposited for it to be fully applicable. this involves particular amendments to the convention’s annexes that must be finalised in a rapid procedure, to enable the convention to enter into force in the whole of the european union. i hope that these procedural steps will be taken as soon as possible.
in writing. − the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance was signed on behalf of the european union by tibor navracsics, the then eu president, minister of administration and justice of hungary in 2011. the convention establishes a common legal framework between eu and non-eu countries to enable authorities to cooperate more effectively in the enforcement of maintenance claims and to prevent debtors from evading their obligations by leaving the territory of the union. it also provides free legal aid in child support cases and simplifies procedures for the recognition and enforcement of court decisions. i therefore vote in favour of the convention being brought into force as soon as possible throughout the european union in the interests of citizens.

in writing. − the visa facilitation procedure has been in force since 1 january 2008 and has proved to be extremely successful, with a very low rejection rate of only 3.3% over the last 5 years. the main elements of the current changes include the welcome extension of the simplified visa regime to ukrainian citizens attending sporting and educational events, international exhibitions and conferences. this is also a significant contribution to eu tourism, as the number of ukrainian visitors increased by 40% between 2010 and 2012 compared to hungary alone, and this is now expected to grow even more dynamically. the commission has also proposed to amend the rules on the application of the emergency fee, so that biometric passport holders can benefit from this preferential scheme. finally, it should be noted that the revision and further relaxations are extremely important for hungary, since there is a hungarian minority in transcarpathia of 150 thousand people. these measures also help their relations with their motherland, since a small border crossing permit or a hungarian passport is not a solution for everyone. all these positive changes made me happy to vote in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. − on thursday, i was pleased to vote in favour of the moraes report on the amendment of the visa agreement between the european union and ukraine. the main objective is to further simplify the procedure for issuing visas for ukrainian and transcarpathian hungarian journalists, civilians and young people, who will now have easier access to uniform eu visas for short-term stays. the amendment initiated in 2011 was approved by the council in 2012, to which the european parliament gave its consent by this vote. cheaper, faster and simpler visa issuance is particularly important for the mobility of young people. the eu has also been active in the field of human rights since the early 1990s, and has been active in the field of human rights since the early 2000s. many studies have shown that free movement is the most important achievement of the union for european citizens, for young people. today, citizens of ukraine, including transcarpathian hungarians, are one step closer to this community achievement.
in writing. − the visa facilitation agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova could facilitate cooperation between the two parties in the fields of economy, culture and public administration. the long-term objective of the visa liberalisation agreement is to ensure effective border management, crime prevention, management of migration flows and peaceful cooperation with neighbouring countries. i support the approval of the agreement as it provides an opportunity to strengthen the relations between the union and the republic of moldova.
in writing. − as the economic and social policies of the eu continue to become more and more complex, there is growing need for reliable statistical data on the trends and dynamics of european demography. the accuracy and substantiation of such data define a long range of eu measures. the decision-making procedure of the union itself relies on the highest possible quality demographical data, but they are also an essential indicator for measuring the sustainability of public finances. time series publications of national statistical offices and the eurostat - for example on life expectancy, fertility rates and age dependency ratios - are a crucial instrument for adjusting social inclusion and development policies as well as for the monitoring of the achievements of all strategies aiming at social inclusion and cohesion.

in writing. the promotion of renewable energy is of strategic importance for europe's competitiveness. the use of green energy not only benefits from a climate protection perspective, but also reduces the union's fossil energy imports and stimulates the economy. thanks to the efforts made so far, the use of renewable energy is growing at a planned rate, with the expectation that by 2020 20% of europe's energy consumption will be covered by renewable energy sources. the increase in green energy is also creating unexpected problems for energy market players. the increasing share of solar and wind energy in the grid, which is subject to weather-related fluctuations, poses a new challenge for transmission system operators in terms of security of supply. in several member states, the rapid growth of renewable energy generation is also hampered by the inability of national grid development investments to keep pace. delayed infrastructure developments increase the risk of transmission networks becoming overloaded, causing disruption to energy supply. in the absence of adequate infrastructure, renewable energy production not only burdens the national grid but also the transmission system of neighbouring member states, causing significant losses to market players in those member states. further infrastructure development and closer eu cooperation are needed to address the problems that have arisen. this is the only way to ensure that renewable energy production does not become the driving force behind the creation of the single energy market, but becomes a success story for the union.

the next item is the debate on the oral question to the commission on the voluntary permanent relocation scheme of the union, tabled by mr juan fernando lópez aguilar on behalf of the committee on citizens' rights, home affairs and justice. the commission shall be assisted by the standing committee on plants, animals, food and feed.
on behalf of the author (mr lópez aguilar). − mr president, mr lópez aguilar has asked me as vice-chair to take the floor on his behalf as chair of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe). on 21 february the libe committee voted on an oral question to be addressed to the commission. the libe committee is concerned about the absence so far of any initiative by the commission relating to the establishment of a voluntary permanent relocation scheme. allow me to remind you briefly of the history of relocation and the importance that our parliament has always attached to relocation, especially in the context of intra-eu solidarity. relocation is the process whereby beneficiaries of international protection are transferred from one member state to another member state, where they will immediately be granted equivalent protection. it is an expression of solidarity for member states that face specific and disproportionate pressure on their asylum and reception system, due in particular to their geographic and demographic situation. in october 2008 the european council endorsed the concept of intra-eu relocation of beneficiaries of international protection. in may 2009, the european commissioner for justice and home affairs, at that time jacques barrot, launched the proposal for a pilot project for relocation from malta, called eurema. it was the first multilateral intra-eu relocation initiative. in view of the influx of asylum seekers from libya and the pressure faced by malta in april 2011, on a proposal from commissioner cecilia malmström this pilot project was extended. the european asylum support office (easo), moreover, has among its tasks to promote, facilitate and coordinate exchanges of information and other activities related to relocation within the union. in its communication in december 2011 on enhanced intra-eu solidarity, the commission expressed again its strong support for relocation of beneficiaries of international protection within the union and undertook to propose a voluntary permanent relocation scheme in 2012, subject to a further impact assessment by the easo. the impact assessment, delivered as a fact-finding report on intra-eu relocation activities from malta, was concluded by easo in 2012. in its conclusion on 8 march 2012, the council clearly stated that further steps on the voluntary relocation within the eu of beneficiaries of international protection should be examined and taken in light of the lessons learnt. the justice and home affairs council of 25 and 26 october 2012 informally discussed the whole issue of the eurema project. in its resolution of 11 september 2012 on enhanced intra-eu solidarity in the field of asylum, parliament called for a proposal for a permanent intra-eu relocation mechanism. it urged the commission to give consideration in its legislative proposal to the use of an eu distribution key for relocation of beneficiaries of international protection, based on appropriate indicators. since then, however, there have been no signs that the commission is ready to come forward with its promised proposal for a voluntary, permanent union relocation scheme. my question is simple and straightforward: when does the commission intend to publish such a proposal to fulfil its commitment of december 2011?

joint debate on the following report and recommendation: report by andrew duff on behalf of the committee on constitutional affairs on the draft protocol on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to the czech republic (article 48 (3) of the treaty on european union) [00091/2011 - c7-0385/2011 to 2011/0817 (nle)) (a7-0174/2013) and recommendation by andrew duff on behalf of the committee on constitutional affairs: proposal for a european council decision on the convening of a convention to be established in order to annex the protocol on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to the czech republic to the treaty on european union and to the treaty on the functioning of the european union [00091/2011 to c7-038/2016 to 2011/0818 (nle)) (a7-0282/2012)
on behalf of the ppe group. – i will continue in english. my thanks to mr duff for all the work that he has put in, and with whose exposé i very largely agree. bringing this report to a conclusion has, of course, been a very slow process. i think all the members of the committee on constitutional affairs are aware of this. it has been with us for about 18 months. the arrival of the report on the czech protocol in plenary has obviously taken time and the deliberations in committee have been complex: sometimes conflicting, sometimes not. there is a reason for this. it seems to me that a whole range of interests have been integrated into the text which is to be voted on this week. this has not been an easy pastime. the story of the protocol, as we have heard from mr duff, goes back to the promise made to the then president of the czech republic that his country could have an opt-out from the charter of fundamental rights. this was evidently a political move with political motivations: basically a gesture to secure that country’s ratification of the lisbon treaty, about which the aforementioned president was more than somewhat hesitant. if the politics of the situation require a gesture of this kind, the legal arrangements point in a different direction. indeed, one of the more illuminating propositions to emerge from this long discussion in committee is that politics and the law do not invariably go in tandem but can point in very different directions. this obviously adds to complexity, not to say confusion. we basically have an opt-out which is not an opt-out, which seems to me to be more than somewhat contradictory. the problem here, i would suggest, is that the legal utility of the opt-out is very much in question, with the consequence that there is, or was, a political promise that has precious little import in real terms. furthermore – and i think this is also highly significant – the political configuration in the czech republic has also changed, with the result that the significance of the political promise has declined from the czech perspective as well. in effect, politics is catching up with the law. for all these reasons i would like to suggest that the rational option for parliament, which of course is obliged to express a view on the czech protocol, is to follow the rapporteur.
