the rapporteur. − firstly, i would like to congratulate my colleague kleva kekuš on her work as my co-rapporteur, and secondly, i would like to thank my shadow rapporteurs and all my colleagues for contributing with their amendments to the completion of my report. most eu member states have adopted very stringent consolidation measures as a response to the crisis. at the same time, it has tried and tried to reduce its debt and has introduced tax changes that may contribute to its success, but in many cases narrow the scope of tax exemption. but at the same time, it's getting stronger, and i would say that it's almost an industry, the institution of tax evasion, and i think that double non-taxation and aggressive tax planning is a problem that needs to be addressed. these factors severely reduce the ability of member states to raise taxes and, moreover, threaten fair taxation. i should mention that the eu's shadow economy is now so large that the commission has indicated that it accounts for almost a fifth of our gdp. that, ladies and gentlemen, is equivalent to two billion euros, which is another aggravating factor. it's also an open secret that billions of euros are hidden in tax havens, which is a problem, and unfortunately, the european union is helping. i have to say that the measures taken so far have not been adequate or have not been sufficiently effective. today, in the light of all this, it is very, very important for the council meeting to have a united position and it is very important that we can formulate a good message, precisely against the tax evaders and their helpers. the analysis shows that tax evasion and avoidance in the eu, as discussed in the debate, amounts to over eur 1 trillion. every loophole in the internal market opens up new and new loopholes for those seeking to avoid taxation. my fellow mps, this is a competition, and at the moment, it is the fraudsters who are winning this competition against the honest taxpayers. that is why this issue must be put on the agenda and why this issue must be discussed. the current crisis has raised serious problems which have required adjustments to national tax policies. in support of this work, my report proposes the development of an intelligent and coordinated tax information system which, instead of harmonising the tax systems of the member states, creates cooperation and coordination in the form of a platform where tax information can be collected, analysed and used for decisions in the next period. i think it is extremely important that the commission should develop the form of information exchange as soon as possible and provide the necessary support. however, fiscal measures and incentives that have an upward impact on the economy should be introduced in parallel with the crisis response. priority should be given to taxes that stimulate economic growth and employment policies in the short, medium and long term. i do not think that new taxes should be imposed or new taxes introduced in this respect. i think it's more important to increase the taxpayer base. at the same time, it is important to act to tackle the problems of tax evasion and avoidance. in this connection, the gaps in the law which some people use as an excuse for not paying the fair tax burden must be closed, as i propose in my report. i would like to conclude by saying, mr president, that i consider the introduction of reverse taxation to be a very good way of reducing vat fraud. however, i have to say that, unfortunately, the commission does not give adequate support to requests from member states in this respect. i ask the commission to change its position on this.
i am glad that the council is dealing with the energy issue in addition to tax havens. now is the time to make some important decisions about one of the biggest fixed costs for businesses and citizens, energy. we know what needs to be done at eu level to ensure a secure energy supply from fewer raw materials and with greater efficiency. but what do we do? we know that we need to connect networks at eu level to reduce our external dependence and improve investment sentiment. but what do we do? we know that large-scale infrastructure investment is needed, because there is a high cost of delay. but what do we do? we know the lengthy approval procedures we've encountered in using the funds we voted for in the 2008 recovery program. but what do we do? we know there's a delay in the transfer of the third power pack. we know that the institutions responsible for this are underfunded. but what do we do? we know that in the digital age, access to energy is a matter of being or not being. but what do we do? we know, but what do we do? the responsibility is historic. if we fail, we'll have to decide whether to invest about a trillion euros or not. this amount is the same as that negotiated in the context of tax havens.
in order to keep energy prices under control, the single energy market should be established as soon as possible. despite the efforts made so far, there are still many regions in the union where there is still not enough physical connectivity and the single market is not functioning. this is why the energy markets in the cee region are also characterised by unilateral energy dependence and higher energy prices than the eu average. the establishment of the single market does not require further legislation at union level, as the 2nd and 3rd energy packages provide a suitable basis for the establishment of the union energy market. the infrastructure package adopted in march this year is also an important step forward in ensuring the smooth flow of energy. however, citizens are still not fully benefiting from the benefits of the single market, as member states are unfortunately far behind in transposing eu law. despite the consumer protection provisions of the energy package 3, energy bills remain complex and do not provide an answer to why energy prices have increased significantly in recent times. regulation is also too permissive in several member states, so that energy suppliers are not obliged to provide consumers with an adequate level of information. in this context, i am convinced that the development of the eu infrastructure, the implementation in the member states and effective market surveillance are the key to ensuring that the acquis is not just abstract legislation for eu citizens, but tangible results. i believe that the council meeting which begins tomorrow is a good opportunity for the leaders of the member states of the european union to reach agreement on these important issues.

mr president, despite all the goodwill speeches and statements, the pressing issues of growth and unemployment – especially youth unemployment – have yet to be properly addressed. one thing is clear though: the austerity-only measures have failed economically, socially and democratically. now is the time for member states to take their responsibilities and put aside short-sighted views. european citizens need more than small steps from one council to another. we have several tools on the table, such as the growth pact or the youth unemployment scheme proposals, but there is no point if these are not followed by concrete measures and implementation as soon as possible. it is time for member states to understand that these measures are much more than spending. it is an investment for the future, for our youth and for the millions of european citizens facing growing social distress. moreover, as many of my colleagues have underlined, the amounts resulting from a more efficient fight against tax havens could have a huge impact if wisely used. the same goes for the financial transaction tax. these are legitimate and fair demands that could have a sustainable and positive effect in building the future of europe.

madam president, the crisis again revealed the extreme fragility of the banking system. in addition to being a market failure, the global financial crisis can be considered a government failure: misguided monetary policies, lack of regulation or distorted regulation. this contributed enormously to the deterioration of asset quality in banks. there is much discussion today about the origins of the crisis, whether it started in the banking system and then spilled over to the fiscal sector after bank rehabilitation, or vice versa. this is a fruitless debate. as long as government policy considers systemic banks too big to fail, there will be no way to cut the link between banking and the financial crisis. to cut the interlinkages between the fiscal and the banking crisis a preannounced schedule of a strong bail-in mechanism is needed, instead of the ad hoc bail-ins and comprehensive bailouts applied so far. no single supervisory mechanism will be credible without a transparent, predictable, rule-based commitment to sharing losses in the event of insolvency. this is not only an economic imperative but also a political one. it is no longer acceptable to privatise profits via socialised losses at the expense of taxpayers. the fundamental rules of capitalism should prevail. monetary policy and banking supervision can get into conflict when it comes to the rehabilitation of individual banks. the supervisory authority must be able to distinguish clearly between temporary problems in liquidity, and insolvency. the monetary authority is expected to discharge its role as lender of last resort only in the case of solvent banks. insolvent banks must not benefit even from temporary liquidity assistance. hence, while the monetary and supervisory functions have to be separated, there is also a need for cooperation and coordination between the two. there are also too many cooks in the kitchen now – the ecb, the eba, the esrb, the efsf, etc. we have to make sure that they all have tasks and responsibilities which are very precisely defined and understood, so that cooperation between them is smooth, rapid, effective and efficient.
the economic crisis has shown us how fragile our banking system is. it also pointed out that the problems of the affected banks in one member state can easily spill over to other member states and that individual solutions cannot and have not been successful. it was time to think of a solution. the achievement of all the elements of banking union can be beneficial for the euro area member states and beyond precisely because it will strengthen the trust that the market always values positively. overall, euro area banks will be able to finance the real economy with less funding, and this could have a positive spillover effect outside the euro area. hungary, together with the visegrád four, takes the view that the measures to create a banking union must not circumvent the existing institutional framework of the eu, place non-euro area countries at a disadvantage or jeopardise the unity of the internal market. i thank mrs marianne thyssen and my colleague mr giegold for the proper handling of these issues and the consideration of the interests of both euro-zone and non-euro-zone member states in the final compromises. i also think it is important that those who want to join this union later on should have a balance of rights and obligations. i also agree that it's a great idea to create a special financial stronghold, and maybe it would be useful for countries outside the euro area. this three-tiered system of supervision is important, but i would like to warn you about it and ask that it not be bureaucratic and that there be no overlapping of powers. in addition, it is also necessary to seek various institutional and financial guarantees. it's a very interesting question for mother and daughter banks to ask. i do not think it is acceptable for foreign-owned subsidiaries to be converted into branches. these two categories represent different national supervisory jurisdictions. mr president, one last sentence: there are still questions to be clarified, they are very important, but we must not rush. thank you again for this report and for the shared thinking that has emerged.

in writing. the transatlantic free trade area between the european union and the united states of america is vital for the european union. in many ways, this could be the realization of a dream that's been around for over 30 years. in view of the difficult economic conditions, the establishment of this agreement is a matter of great urgency, as this agreement is the key to launching economic growth in both the european union and the united states. a free trade agreement can open up new markets for europe, increase foreign direct investment and, as a result, create many value-adding jobs and increase europe's competitiveness on the world market. it could improve europe's exports by up to 28% and the us's exports by 37% with gdp growth in both countries continuing at a steady rate of up to 0.5% per year. the agreement on fuels and chemicals would be particularly beneficial, as it would develop industry and the energy market, thereby providing european citizens with cheaper energy. the agreement would also serve to develop global regulations to strengthen the multilateral trading system. it is important to emphasise that europe, not the united states, should set the standards in this area. to seek what unites and understand what separates. that could be the key to success in the negotiations.
in writing. i welcome the efforts to develop a macro-regional strategy for the alps. i believe that macro-regional strategies have a significant added value, as they seek to build on existing financial resources to achieve development by making better use of synergies. the two existing macro-regional strategies (baltic and danube) have shown that society is highly receptive to macro-regional cooperation. bottom-up construction, multi-level governance, and stakeholder mobilisation already in the strategy-making phase will enable macro-regional strategies to offer solutions tailored to the needs of the regions. while the usefulness of such strategies is unquestionable, i believe it is important that the evaluation of existing strategies be carried out as soon as possible, on the basis of full, objective criteria and measurable indicators. the danube strategy adopted during the hungarian presidency focused on sustainable development, creating a livable, environmentally friendly danube region. sustainable development should be a key element of any future macro-regional strategy. given that macro-regional strategies can effectively contribute to the europe 2020 strategy and the objectives of sustainable development, and also promote the active involvement of society and stakeholders in all phases of the strategy, i believe that more attention should be paid to these strategies in the future.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the revision of the rules on the transport of pet animals has created conditions which will make it easier for european citizens to travel with their pets in the future without any particular difficulties or interpretation problems. in order to prevent circumvention, the previous commission regulation (eu) no 388/2010 limited the maximum number of animals that could be transported in this way to five, which in practice caused a number of undue difficulties for those wishing to participate in sporting events, competitions and exhibitions. a further problem was the divergent approach of the member states with regard to the compulsory vaccination against rabies of animals less than 3 months of age. finally, the rules on the filling in of identification documents have often caused confusion among veterinarians and owners. the amendment has now resolved all these problems and i congratulate the rapporteur on the agreement reached at first reading.

on behalf of the ppe group. as coordinator of the pp, i would like to congratulate elisabeth morin-chartier and welcome the fact that an agreement has been reached with the council at first reading. as we know, the union has exclusive legislative competence in the field of health and safety at work. this is not a coincidence, since it is a matter of protecting human life and health, and there is of course an economic aspect: from the point of view of competition law, it ensures that economic operators compete on the same terms. magnetic resonance is a physical phenomenon, a set of physical effects that workers encounter quite often in the workplace, and therefore protection is warranted. at the same time, it is important to know that this always costs money, so there are serious economic interests in the background. so it's really important to have a balance, a balanced approach, and to have all the legislators negotiate with everybody. if we don't do that, we're making the mistake that we made in 2004, probably, of not recognizing that between the health interest and the economic interest, there's another social interest, namely the interest of healthy healing. these are technical means which the legislator did not intend to exclude. so once again i can say that the ppe supports this report and welcomes the rapporteur's work in achieving a good, healthy balance on this issue.
in writing. - mr president, i have to go. today's debate is for many the joyous end of a long journey. medical circles first sounded the alarm in 2006 when it emerged that an earlier directive regulating the exposure of workers to risks arising from exposure to electromagnetic fields would have inadvertently restricted the use and development of the magnetic resonance imaging technique, more commonly known as mri. as we all know, mri scans are one of the most important tools in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer and other serious diseases. europe is a leader in research and development of technology, and thus also provides the highest quality of healthcare for its patients. without the unprecedented european convergence of patient organisations, researchers and doctors, as well as politicians, which is forcing the amendment of the directive that is now before us, the possibilities for medical application and technical development of mri would have been seriously jeopardised. after the parties had demonstrated during the negotiations that the health sector had already taken care to introduce strict precautions with regard to the risks to workers, the use of mri was finally exempted from the very strict exposure limits of the directive. i would like to congratulate all my colleagues who have contributed to this report. i believe that in more than seven years of fighting for the future of the irm, the european parliament has once again succeeded in proving that european citizens can count on the help of their elected representatives.

in writing. − the council directive on legal aid for crossborder disputes has been in force since 2003, but relatively few citizens and legal practitioners are aware of the rights and benefits it provides. the directive is primarily intended to promote access to justice in another member state for the less well-off members of society, for example when exercising their right to free movement. the experience of recent years has shown that an effective information campaign should be launched in all member states in order to ensure that citizens have as wide a range of recourse to the legal aid in cross-border disputes as possible. given that legal aid and training of experts involve costs for member states and that in the current economic environment the financing of such services may be limited in many member states, we call on the commission to provide, where possible, specific resources to ensure that member states are able to provide high-level legal training in legal aid matters.

in writing. − enhancing occupational mobility is one of the significant challenges that the eu faces in developing its labour market. education and training systems in all member states need to be adapted to meet the requirement of the job market and the knowledge-based society. although the economic crisis resulted in the dismantling of many workplaces, there are over two million unfilled vacancies in the eu because there are no workers with the required skills in the local job market. complementing the formal education system, extensive vocational education and training are necessary therefore to acquire the cross-cutting skills that are most sought after in the labour market. it is important especially in the case of women who leave their jobs temporarily for childbirth and taking care of their families and find it extremely difficult to return to the labour market. most member states failed to implement on-the-job training opportunities and, as a result, many individuals leave jobs – including public employment – without any additional skills. vocational training must therefore not only be easily accessible and career-oriented but must also incorporate a strong focus on work-based learning to facilitate the transition of young women – especially those with disadvantages – to the workforce.

mr president, commissioner, i am quite certain that everyone in this house fully supports media freedom as an essential condition of a properly functioning democracy. the media possess the power to call to account other actors in the political process. what the report does not touch on, though, is what happens when the media do not use their power with full attention to the responsibility that goes with power; the power to move public opinion, for example, and the power to act in a quasi-judicial capacity. this problem of accountability is rather less important in countries without democracy or where democracy is under attack. there, what the media do is vital in sustaining civil society and making public information that the rulers prefer to keep secret. but the situation is much less straightforward in societies with a strong democratic infrastructure. there the media must act with a markedly higher standard of responsibility precisely because they operate in a democratic environment. yet journalism in democratic society has changed. i speak as a former journalist. the media are less discerning, less committed to original investigative journalism and are much less motivated to keep clear blue water between reporting and passing judgment. all in all, there is every reason for the media to be subject to the same rules of democracy that all other political actors must observe.

in writing. − the new legislation aims to increase road safety, reduce administrative burdens and simplify previous rules. the proposal provides for more precise definitions of the place of registration of vehicles than are currently in force and introduces the concept of withdrawal and cancellation of marketing authorisations. the coating would ensure that vehicles which pose a direct risk to road safety are not allowed to use the roads: the registration of such vehicles would be withdrawn until the next technical inspection has been successfully completed. furthermore, vehicles which are re-registered in another member state are automatically deleted from the original register. this will avoid the same vehicle being registered in several member states at the same time. vehicles which are declared to be scrapped on the basis of the periodic technical inspection or which have reached the end of their useful life shall be removed from the register following notification. the proposal also lays down new requirements for electronic registration systems and for the monitoring of the results of technical inspections, vehicle re-registration and dismantling.
in writing. − the paperwork for vehicles is a considerable burden for citizens. the proposal will make the implementation of the roadworthiness and roadworthiness testing system more efficient. in order to reduce the administrative burden, vehicles re-registered in another member state shall be automatically deleted from the original register. the proposal contains new requirements for electronic registration systems and for the monitoring of the results of technical inspections, vehicle re-registration and dismantling. the rapporteur proposes some amendments to reduce the number of papers drivers have to carry with them at all times. it also supports the creation of electronic databases and would like these national databases to be linked to those of other member states in order to facilitate vehicle identification. with the balkan states joining, it seems very useful to reduce the chance of our cars becoming tar, so i voted for it.
in writing. − the report on the roadworthiness of commercial vehicles is part of the technical suitability of vehicles package. the stated policy objective of the document is to substantially improve road safety, i.e. to reduce the number of fatal road accidents by 50% between 2010 and 2020. this legislation aims to achieve this by means of: introducing a risk assessment system for the selection of vehicles to be inspected; more annual technical inspections and regularly coordinated inspection activities in the member states; extending road checks to cargo (improper loading of cargo is responsible for 25% of all accidents involving trucks); adequate training of inspectors, etc. increasing european road safety is a highly important political objective, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − the possibilities of the current control system are not being used properly by our authorities, because their aim is not to improve safety, but to prevent fraud and enterprises. vehicles in bad technical condition, foreigners who are speeding and breaking the rules, are not afraid to stop, or are simply not willing to be stopped by our average police officers or the people of the transport authority who do not know a word of foreign languages. this material is a step forward in that it encourages testing of more accident-prone vehicles, while small trucks typically used by small businesses under 3.5 tonnes would not be unduly harassed. i voted no on the points that reduce national competence, yes on the whole. if we take advantage of these new opportunities, our roads will be safer, if not, the situation will be better, because foreign vehicles will also have to be inspected.
in writing. − the report on the technical examination of motor vehicles and their trailers is part of the package of legislation on the technical suitability of vehicles. the stated policy objective of the document is to substantially improve road safety, i.e. to reduce the number of fatal road accidents by 50% between 2010 and 2020. this legislation aims to achieve this by means of: inter alia mandatory eu-wide roadworthiness tests for scooters and motorcycles; increasing the frequency of periodic roadworthiness tests; improving the quality of roadworthiness tests by establishing common minimum standards for defects and equipment; reducing mileage fraud by recording mileage; making electronic safety devices mandatory for testing, etc. increasing european road safety is a highly important political objective, which is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. − the report deals with the types of state aid provided for in articles 90 to 94 of the treaty of lisbon. the essence of this is that the union's objectives must be achieved within the framework of a common aid policy. the details are set out in regulation (ec) no 994/98, which empowers the commission to grant exemptions from the control of aid in certain areas. these include amateur sports, tourism, research and development, and some areas of innovation. the report aims to exempt from commission scrutiny aid that is in line with the europe 2020 priorities. the proposals given give greater latitude to the policy of the nation state, which is why i had to vote for the report.

in writing. rui tavares' latest amendment this time targets the hungarian national security law, claiming that the stricter screening procedure than before seriously threatens the rule of law. the national security law, as amended by the hungarian parliament, imposes stricter screening requirements than before on senior officials of state bodies under the supervision of the government, primarily law enforcement leaders. however, judges, in general prosecutors, the presidents of the curia and the office of the judge, are not subject to the extended review procedure. the only exceptions are judges and prosecutors who make decisions about intelligence operations. the increased scrutiny is intended to stem the rampant corruption and moral decay that has reached the police, among others, during eight years of socialist rule. tavares feared the law, the principle of separation of powers, while other left-liberal representatives directly envisioned the collapse of the rule of law and the abolition of the right to privacy. in reality, however, the posts subject to scrutiny have not changed and concern only those people in positions who know in advance what they are undertaking. the scrutiny of the matter is strictly a matter for the member states under the eu treaties, as exemplified by the fact that scrutiny mechanisms are radically different in each member state. so rui tavares has again called out wolves where, unfortunately, no orphaned wolves roam.

mr. president, colleagues, ladies and gentlemen, first of all, i'd like to thank both of you for your work. at this stage of the debate, i would like to draw the attention of my colleagues to three considerations which have perhaps not received sufficient attention in the discussions so far. first of all, i would like to point out that the introduction of thresholds by olaf in setting its priorities for investigations in 2012-13 is a cause for concern in the fight against fraud. the office examines the likely financial impact of each case on a case-by-case basis and, if it does not reach a certain value, olaf is unlikely to investigate the case. the thresholds set are very high, for example in the customs sector and the european regional development fund, and irregularities below eur 1 million are not considered to be a significant case of fraud by the office. secondly, i regret the fact that more than half of the olaf investigations that went to the judicial stage between 2006 and 2011 have not yet resulted in a judicial decision. last but not least, one of the most effective ways to reduce vat and tax fraud would be to link commercial transactions in real time with the tax authorities. i'm glad the report brings that to the fore.
mr. chairman, members of the house of representatives, i would like to highlight two important areas. one is the customs issue. 70% of customs procedures in the union are carried out under the simplified procedure. the findings of the court of auditors' special report no 1/2010 are of particular concern as they point to serious shortcomings in this area. the use of advanced information systems would be necessary to reduce the evasibility of the authorities, and i therefore believe that it is essential to make uniform and full use of the modernised customs code as soon as possible. the second is cigarette smuggling, which costs member states' budgets €10 billion a year. it's basically funding the operations of various criminal organizations, which is completely unacceptable. member states raise taxes on tobacco products to reduce the number of smokers, but in the meantime it is essential to tighten controls, as tax increases clearly push things in the direction of smuggling. in sum, it is in the common interest of all of us that the competent agencies and authorities should be able to detect fraud as much as possible, if only to help honest governments and honest businesses.

in writing. − following the commission's proposal, this material is welcome to propose strengthening the ucits system in terms of delegation of deposit-keeping activities, liability, remuneration, sanctions, and consumer protection. the draft rightly states that, since investment in ucits involves significant risks, the risks must be directly linked to the investments and not to the transfer of the depositary activity or the limited liability of the management of the ucits in order to guarantee the protection of retail investors in an absolute manner. in the area of remuneration, the main objective is to ensure consistency between the different financial instruments and the legislation. it is appropriate to establish that the scope of the remuneration scheme for employees should cover all decision-making staff in both the ucits and the management company. it is also true that it is desirable to introduce certain changes in the fund managers in order to make them work more efficiently, as the performance fee paid to the fund managers rarely improves the performance of the fund and therefore the variable remuneration should be proportionate to the size of the fund or the value of the assets managed. it is encouraging that, in addition to remuneration, the draft also addresses the issue of sanctions, which will help to minimise market abuse and will allow the imposition of proportionate and dissuasive administrative fines in the future. the plan is comprehensive and thorough, i recommend it for support!
in writing. − if we want to live in a livable world, the amount of real and virtual money in circulation should match the volume of real goods and services exchanged. today, the virtual something called money lives on its own and generates extra profits through speculative methods for certain circles primarily. however, even legally acquired savings, such as money from pension funds, are now managed by such speculative investment funds. this amendment, which amends directive 2009/65/ec, provides for uniform rules on the authorisation, supervision, organisation and activities of investment funds and the information which they are required to disclose. until now, managers of such investment companies have been encouraged to pursue the highest possible risk for the highest possible profit, since if they failed, the investors were relieved by the state from the burden of taxpayers. we condemn all speculative activity, but this is the fate of people's pensions, which they have earned throughout their lives, and this amendment should be supported because it represents a decisive step forward compared to the previous ones.

on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, my congratulations to mr duff. i think that the work on this particular dossier has been excellent. the thrust of this report is to ensure that the elections to the european parliament next year are held with a maximum of success. at the same time, the report also wants to ensure that these are, to the extent that is possible, european elections with the stress on european. we know from the past that national issues tend to hijack the european dimension of these elections. a consequence of this is that the turnout is less than satisfactory and that voters have been known to use the european elections as a protest vote, assuming that what happens in the european parliament is secondary. we here know that this is a misreading of the situation, but the voters are less clear on the issue. to remedy this, the assumption is that european level political parties will play an enhanced role in the elections and crucially that they will nominate candidates for the presidency of the commission. the logic is that thereby the next president of the commission will enjoy greater legitimacy and be more accountable to the citizens of europe. this step further means that a european-level campaign will be held – should be held – in order to maximise the awareness of the citizens of europe that politics today is more than national. the main point here is that over the years a good deal of power has migrated from the member states to the european union on a variety of grounds – effectiveness, the interdependence of the states of europe, the integration of many functions. this process also signifies that it is vital that the power of the european union be fully legitimated at the level at which it is exercised, the european level. next year’s elections should be a key step in that direction.
mr president, we are all aware of the very high stakes associated with the next european elections. one of the major challenges will be to ensure a genuine european debate. we may disagree politically, but i am sure that we can all agree that european citizens deserve a campaign which clearly outlines the common challenges that europe is facing and the different political alternatives. it is also crucial to strengthen the transparency and democratic legitimacy of the european union which has suffered from the way the crisis has been handled so far. as representatives of the citizens, members of the european parliament have a crucial role to play; in particular since the european parliament has been granted extended powers with the treaty of lisbon. having a common candidate for the presidency of the european commission will help to defend the different european political programmes. we call on the council to duly take into account the results of the election when nominating the candidate for the crucial position – as provided for in the lisbon treaty. therefore i fully support the provisions contained in the report of mr duff and i sincerely hope that member states will make the necessary arrangements which will strengthen the democratic life of the european union. furthermore, let me underline the importance of having candidates who represent the european society in its diversity. it is paramount to have women, young people and people from minorities running for the elections at an appropriate position on the list. when it comes to women, we are still far from parity; a clear signal must be sent and this is a matter of democracy. parliament has to lead by example when it comes to gender equality and, as a shadow rapporteur of the report on european political parties, i am strongly in favour, dear viviane reding, of european parties having a status. let us hope that the lithuanian presidency will bring it about, and i note their absence at this crucial debate.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, as it proposes to reduce borrowers' risk appetite, regulate the maximum repayment amount, the possibility of changing interest rates, the convertibility of foreign currency loans, and introduce reflection time, personalised advice and the requirement of traceability. it also ensures that home buyers across the eu are better informed and better illustrated about the risks of mortgages, the increase in the repayment instalment due to exchange rate fluctuations and even better protected in the event of a loan default. meps included in the rules the possibility of early repayment of loans without penalty and the possibility of their fair conversion into another currency. the stock of retail foreign currency loans in hungary is one of the largest, which may have developed because bankers, instead of warning about the real risks of foreign currency lending, even chased borrowers into taking irresponsible risks. foreign currency credit is like a defective product that the seller would have to replace or repair in some form, which a uniform eu-wide regulation and support could further promote.
in writing. − the stock of retail foreign currency loans in hungary is one of the largest, which may have developed because bankers, instead of warning about the real risks of foreign currency lending, even encouraged borrowers to take irresponsible risks. the report adopted today calls for an end to this irresponsible practice at eu level. the proposal requires that home buyers throughout the european union receive more thorough and illustrated information on the risks of mortgages, the increase in the payment instalment due to exchange rate fluctuations and greater protection in the event of default. the report shall include early repayment of the loan without penalty and the possibility of its fair conversion into another currency. i voted in favour of the proposal as it reduces the risk exposure of borrowers, regulates the maximum repayment amount, the possibility of changing interest rates, the convertibility of foreign currency loans, and introduces reflection time, personalised advice and traceability as an expectation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, which aims to establish a common framework at european level and is well suited to the current regulatory framework for financial transactions. the report includes all financial instruments, including algorithmic trading and high frequency trading (hft), under common supervision, i.e. extending market protection to both primary and unregulated spot markets. it is crucial for everyday life that the proof of individual intent is no longer required for the determination of manipulation or negative market behaviour, but that in future it will be sufficient to establish a link between the behaviour of an individual that gives rise to the abuse and the financial instruments in question, even indirectly. it is also a positive step that the report requires that all organised trading is actually carried out on venues subject to the same conditions as regards transparency, organisation and market surveillance.
in writing. − the single energy market is the key to ensuring that consumers have access to energy at affordable prices and without interruption. i voted in favour of the report as it proposes concrete solutions to address the shortcomings that exist. of these, i consider the following three proposals to be particularly important: first, the unexpected difficulty in several member states was that national grid development investments could not keep up with the rapid growth of renewable energy generation. loop flows are frequent and cause a load on the transmission system of neighbouring member states. i therefore agree that there is a need for better coordination and faster licensing to build the missing infrastructure. secondly, a significant proportion of eu energy products are internationally traded, which is why supervision at eu level is essential in addition to national supervision of wholesale trade. this presents a new challenge for the european agency for the cooperation of energy regulators and national authorities. i therefore consider it important that the authorities have sufficient resources to carry out their tasks with due diligence. this investment has a multiplier effect, as the cost of detecting one market abuse can be more than the cost of running the agency for a whole year. thirdly, i agree that european gas prices are unreasonably high today. this is partly due to the lack of investments that can offset the surge in renewable energy production. that is why i voted in favour of the efforts to reduce the price of imported gas and to review the indexation of oil prices.
in writing. − i support the initiative to promote energy efficiency, the report sets out the steps taken to strengthen europe's energy efficiency, one of the priorities of the europe 2020 strategy. it is also worth noting that investments in energy efficiency can have significant economic and social benefits for member states, thus helping to increase the union's competitiveness and employment, which is also in line with the objectives of the 2020 strategy. in addition to the positive effects on the business sector, reducing households' energy dependence is also of paramount importance, and i agree that solutions need to be found to encourage investment in improving household energy efficiency.
in writing. − the european union attaches great importance to the cultural and linguistic diversity of its member states and helps citizens to have access to any information of general interest in their own language, be it about the functioning of any of the union's institutions. this means that meps can put forward motions in any of the eu's official languages and speak in the european parliament, which provides official interpretation. however, the multilingualism of parliament is becoming more expensive every year, and translation and interpretation into the 24 official languages of the union already entails costs that require a rethinking of the system. the dutch rapporteur's report contains proposals to make the multilingual system of interpretation and translation more cost-effective and simpler, without causing a reduction in european multilingualism or a decline in the quality of interpretation and translation.
in writing. − in relation to online gambling, particular attention should be paid to the protection of minors and to protecting them from accessing such content. i therefore support the initiative to exchange and share member states' regulations, control methods and experience on such online content and to strengthen cooperation between member states. after all, these activities can easily become addictive and addictive for both adolescents and adults, endangering their financial security. i therefore support the idea that a common regulatory framework is needed for online gambling. as a member of parliament and a sports fan, i agree with the proposal that more effective cooperation at european level is needed to combat match fixing.
in writing. the amount of payment appropriations estimated to be needed by dg r&i in 2014 is eur 4,9 billion. this would ensure the payment of the dividend advance and balance under the existing fp7 grant agreement and, in particular, the pre-financing of new commitments. the current draft budget for 2014 adopted by the commission reduces the amount of payment appropriations for the directorate-general for research and innovation from eur 4,9 billion to eur 3,8 billion. this is a 22% or eur 1.1 billion reduction over the estimates. the draft budget for 2014 will consequently not be sufficient to cover the needs and such a situation will be detrimental to the beneficiaries. the council also approved an administrative cut of eur 14,5 million in commitment and payment appropriations. so far, the council has not explained why it has initiated this cut in staff expenditure. the commission was forced to reduce it because of the constraints on payment appropriations in the mff.

in writing. - i voted for the cult commission's own-initiative report. i agree that one of the fundamental principles of the european union is linguistic and cultural diversity, and that all european languages are equal in their value and dignity. the report also highlights the fact that the official languages of the member states may be endangered languages in different parts of the union. i particularly support the point in the report that the european parliament calls on the governments of the member states to condemn practices that cause linguistic discrimination and forced or covert assimilation. i also agree that languages which have been marginalised and are more likely to be confined to the family circle should enjoy the rights of public social use. finally, i believe that the most important thing to be said is that the commission should pay attention to the fact that, by its policies, some member states and regions are putting at risk the survival of languages within their borders, even if these languages are not threatened at european level.

in writing. − today i was pleased to vote in favour of the european parliament's resolution on endangered languages. the ep has not adopted a report on regional, minority or endangered languages since 2003, which is why today's decision, adopted by a large majority, is important. in my amendments to the report, which were tabled and voted, which i tabled on a number of occasions with regard to the use of the hungarian language by minorities, including the use of the hungarian language by the cypriots, i pointed out that countries should not regard all the languages spoken on their territory as a burden but as a value and an opportunity. i also considered it important to emphasise that a language may be endangered in relation to a particular area if it was historically spoken in that area; therefore, the monitoring of census data is important in this respect. i also considered it essential to emphasise the role of the media and new technologies, which, and their support, can play a major role in the survival, preservation and transmission of endangered languages between generations. according to unesco, more than 100 languages are considered endangered in the european union. the european union and its member states, individually and collectively, have a duty to promote these languages, thus preserving the values inherent in linguistic diversity. if no change is made in this area, further minority languages and communities may be at risk, which is why joint action is important.

in writing. − the committee on petitions offers public assistance to eu citizens who have been affected by a breach of rights or a loss of rights in their own country. however, citizens' complaints also highlight certain weaknesses in the eu's public administration system, such as competency gaps. the committee receives a number of complaints which can only indirectly be the subject of eu standards, such as the situation of minorities. a constant source of frustration for petitioners is that the committee does not have decision-making powers to resolve, for example, the minority dilemma. it may, at the very most, decide that the european commission, which has the power to take a decision, may not close the case in time. the committee on petitions, for example, has the lion's share in putting on the agenda and evaluating the complaint which, in the context of the slovak citizenship law, which severely discriminates against the hungarian minority in the upper peninsula, has highlighted the relativisation of fundamental rights by some member states. legal solutions that amount to a serious breach of fundamental rights applicable to the whole of the union cannot go unanswered by the eu institutions, since trust in public institutions is one of the most important indicators of democracy.
in my view, the fight against climate change can only be successful on a global scale. if the european union unilaterally commits to an ambitious emission reduction target, while other developed countries and large emitters do not commit to similarly ambitious targets, this could be detrimental to the continent in several ways. first, it does not create a comprehensive and legally binding global convention in which each party undertakes to meet its own capabilities. on the other hand, the unequal situation could put the eu at a significant competitive disadvantage, further increasing european energy prices. at the 2009 copenhagen climate summit, the eu made the only ambitious commitment among developed countries, which led to the eu bearing the brunt of the burden alone during the first commitment period of the kyoto protocol, putting its member states at a disadvantage, and unfortunately this situation was also carried over to the second commitment period. it is therefore essential to avoid a similar situation in the context of the new global agreement. therefore, as a hungarian representative, i support the eu making an appropriate commitment under the unfccc, both for the pre-2020 ambition review and for the post-2020 targets, but only if all developed countries and major emitters make a similarly ambitious commitment.

in writing. − as the economic and social policies of the eu continue to become more and more complex, there is a growing need for reliable statistical data on the trends and dynamics of european demography. the accuracy and substantiation of such data define a wide range of eu measures. the decision-making procedure of the union itself relies on the highest possible quality demographical data, but they are also an essential indicator for measuring the sustainability of public finances. time series publications by national statistical offices and eurostat – for example on life expectancy, fertility rates and age dependency ratios – are a crucial instrument in adjusting social inclusion and development policies as well as in monitoring the achievements of all strategies aimed at social inclusion and cohesion. the precise and clear definition of such basic concepts as ‘nationalʼ or ‘regionalʼ is very timely therefore, and so this initiative is to be welcomed.

mr president, the new multiannual financial framework (mff) is a great victory for those political forces which show the greatest level of responsibility about using european taxpayers’ money. several governments in the european council, as well as the ecr group, have stated very clearly from the beginning that in times of deep economic and financial crisis the eu budget cannot grow in size. if national budgets have to shrink – and fiscal consolidation is an integral part of national economic policy – the eu too must adjust its fiscal stance. not that the only thing which matters is the size of the budget: equally important is the structure of the budget. in this respect we cannot be satisfied at all. despite calls for major improvements, the eu budget is still too heavily geared to spending on items which reflect the status quo, as defended by strong vested interests, rather than the future of the european union. the new mff will not change the status quo. it will not make the eu substantially more competitive and productive, and that is a pity. i have made several speeches in this house to draw attention to the fact that the eu budget is a capital budget rather than a current one, and i am glad that everybody now uses the term ‘investment budget’. given its small size compared to national budgets, it cannot, and should not, aspire to reflect the same priorities as national budgets. moreover, if the eu is not to evolve into a superstate, but rather is to remain a light structure for achieving objectives best achieved jointly, then the eu budget should finance almost exclusively investment projects.

ten years ago i was amazed by the work of jan mulder as a speaker, and for the ten years since then i have been involved in budgetary debates. i never thought i'd be sitting at the president's table watching this debate, but i do know that the praise that has been given here is the praise that is deserved. it's not self-praise, it's hard work. it's the future that will decide whether 6% self-discipline is some kind of suicide. i hope that this will not be the case, i hope that this budget will be enforceable and will bring real results for the citizens of europe. i'll close this discussion. the vote will take place on wednesday 20 november 2013. in writing. as the people's party coordinator of the european parliament's committee on employment and social affairs, i welcome the draft 2014 budget and today's debate. i consider it extremely significant that after long negotiations the council and the european parliament have finally reached an agreement and i welcome the fact that, despite the cuts, the commitment appropriations for competitiveness, growth and employment have increased. i would also like to express my satisfaction with the efforts made by both institutions during the negotiations to ensure that the 2014 budget is a stimulus for economic growth and job creation, with a particular focus on young people. the youth employment initiative will thus have a commitment appropriation of eur 3.9 billion and a payment appropriation of eur 900 million to allow the programme to start properly. with regard to the new eu fund for the most deprived, i would also like to express my satisfaction that the amount allocated to the fund has increased from the initial eur 2.5 billion to eur 3.5 billion. the eures programme budget will also be increased under the agreement, which is of great significance as it will also finance the mobility of unemployed young people. however, the european globalisation adjustment fund will unfortunately only have €159 million available in future instead of the previous €500 million commitment appropriation. in addition, it will also have to finance youth unemployment, which was not previously the responsibility of the fund, so that the fund will have to do more with less money.
in writing. − the european parliament gave its consent to the february agreement of the european council of heads of state or government at its plenary session today. this decision will allow the planning of the union's financial period 2014-2020 to start. the european parliament was unable to substantially amend the main headings of the 2014-2020 financial framework in its negotiations with the council. over the next seven years, €960 billion will be available for commitments and €908 billion will be spent on eu programmes. in seven years, we will receive 35.5 billion euros in regional development and agricultural resources. in terms of net position, hungary has the second highest per capita aid in the union. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − i am pleased that the european parliament approved the eu's multiannual financial framework by a large majority at its plenary session in november. it is regrettable that the european parliament has not been able to substantially amend the headings of the 2014-2020 financial framework during the interinstitutional negotiations, so that over the next seven years eur 960 billion will be committed and eur 908 billion will be actually spent on eu programmes. at the same time, the european parliament was able to make progress in the negotiations. eur 2.5 billion is earmarked for 2014 and 2015 for objectives related to youth employment, research under the erasmus programme and support for smes. an additional €1 billion will be available to provide food aid to those most in need. parliament also pushed for a mid-term review of the framework in 2016 to allow for additional resources to be brought into the common budget (if the union's economic performance improves by then). a high-level conciliation body will be set up to reform the system of own resources representing the revenue side of the union budget.
in writing. − the hungarian people's party has been pressing for an agreement with the council as soon as possible to secure the eu funds that will be transferred to hungary between 2014 and 2020 following the european council's agreement in february. we must stand firmly for the acceptance of the compromise, as it serves the interests of both european and hungarian citizens. hungary is one of the biggest beneficiaries of the agreement, receiving more than €35 billion in development and agricultural aid over the next seven years. the adoption of the agreement will allow the new multiannual programmes to start in 2014. the current hungarian government institutional system is ready to launch programmes and effectively draw up the resources, which means that tens of thousands of jobs can be created in hungary in the coming years with the help of subsidies.
in writing. − i am voting in favour of the european parliament adopting the political agreement on the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 and the new interinstitutional agreement. hungary is one of the biggest beneficiaries of the february agreement: the negotiating delegation led by viktor orbán was able to get a bigger slice of the smaller eu pie than the previous socialist government. in seven years, hungary could receive 35.5 billion euros in regional development and agricultural resources, making it the second largest per capita aid recipient in the european union. however, it is important that the mid-term review of the financial framework takes place no later than 2016 so that additional resources can be brought into the common budget if the union's economic performance improves by then.
in writing. − i am pleased that parliament and the council agree on the importance of stimulating economic growth and job creation, especially in the context of the situation of young people. youth unemployment is much higher than that of the adult population. as new graduates with little work experience, they face many obstacles that make placement not only difficult but often impossible. it is therefore particularly important that next year a commitment appropriation of eur 3.9 billion and a payment appropriation of eur 900 million have been agreed for the financing of the youth employment initiative. it is welcome that the new eu fund for the most deprived has increased from the initial €2.5 billion to €3.5 billion. however, it is regrettable that the budget of the european globalisation adjustment fund will be reduced, despite the fact that this fund has very important tasks.
in writing. − the european parliament's plenary today voted by a large majority to adopt the new eu programme for education, training, youth and sport, known as erasmus+. the programme will run for seven years between 2014 and 2020. the most successful and well-known of the union's initiatives, erasmus, enjoying a high level of popularity, can also be continued as a sub-programme of the framework programme, with some 2,3 million students participating in exchange programmes between 1987 and 2011. erasmus+ will bring together a large number of young people, over four million, aged between 13 and 30, in a variety of programmes. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − the erasmus programme, which was set up to support mobility, has helped some 2.3 million students to participate in exchange programmes between 1987 and 2011, so it is fair to say that erasmus is a model for mobility programmes in other sectors of education, vocational training and youth work. as a former minister for sport, i am particularly pleased that sport has been included as an area to be supported in the multiannual financial perspective. the actions proposed in the new programme to support sport are thus in line with the eu sport work plan adopted in 2011 under the hungarian eu presidency.
in writing. − today i voted in favour of the proposal to establish the 'erasmus+' programme in the hope that it will prove to be a suitable instrument for the adequate protection and promotion of national minority and regional languages and endangered languages, as the european commission had previously promised. the european union's education, training, youth and sport programme as its name suggests should really be accessible to everyone, whether the student, learner or even sportsperson is part of a majority or national minority community. it is important to recognise that future support for multilingualism must not only mean support for the learning of the major european languages, but also for the majority of minority and endangered languages and for mutual learning of each other's languages in neighbouring countries. linguistic mobility is not just about a member of a minority community learning the majority language, but also about a member of the majority doing the same, thus also coming closer to the community, understanding it better. i hope that the european commission will also take the initiative to support such programmes. it is also recommended that you exercise caution when listing individual erasmus+ programmes, so that communities speaking endangered languages can apply for funding from erasmus+ despite their small size.
in writing. − i believe that supporting not only students in higher education and vocational training but also adults and the disadvantaged is important. it is a pleasure to see that the erasmus programme has been universally recognised throughout the world. however, he fears that extending the programme beyond higher education could cause confusion in the future. therefore, i propose that the current designations comenius (for school education), erasmus (for higher education), leonardo da vinci (for vocational education), grundtvig (for adult learning) and young people in action (for youth) should be retained and strengthened separately.
in writing. − the ambitious and diverse ‘erasmus for all’ programme may prove one of the most beneficial initiatives of the 2014-2020 programming period and will hopefully inherit the success and popularity of its predecessor strands. the promotion of education in a lifelong learning perspective, including vocational training and adult learning is of major importance and the focus on youth covering also non-formal and informal learning, active citizenship, social inclusion and volunteering is also to be highly welcomed. the programme will hopefully not only improve the level of key competences and skills, but also promote social cohesion and inclusion of vulnerable groups at risk of educational disadvantage as well as safeguard young people coming from a socially disadvantaged background so that they can also benefit from the programme. the major emphasis placed on sports and grassroots sports in particular is very important, and the programme will hopefully increase the number of socially disadvantaged children in competitive and leisure sport activities and furthermore develop sport facilities and opportunities so that disadvantaged children can engage in sport outside school in disadvantaged regions. i also truly hope that the connected european sports day or week promoting the social and cultural role of amateur and professional sport can be realized.

in writing. − i would like to welcome this report and the preparation of the ‘europe for citizens’ programme, which may largely contribute to the development of a european sense of togetherness, through showing the cultural, linguistic and geographical diversity of our union and cultivating our common history. the transmission and research of the diverse historic experiences, values and memories of europe will hopefully firmly promote understanding and peace. i would like to welcome in specific the programme’s focus on minorities including roma, because increasing public awareness of their role in the common european history as well as their vicissitudes may strengthen tolerance and stability. it also very important to give official support to the research into the less well-known chapters of totalitarian atrocities throughout the continent, such as the roma holocaust. the lack of a thorough and honest scientific analysis of the persecutions is an obstacle to facing and atoning for historic sins, and drawing their lessons for the sake of our common future. historical truth and memory however, will reinforce genuine reconciliation between communities, strengthen and peace, and strengthen our unity as free and equal european citizens.
in writing. − the chernobyl accident in 1986 and the fukushima daiichi accident in 2011 showed that a nuclear accident can have a global impact on public health, social life, the environment and the economy that transcends national borders. it is therefore essential that the european union prioritise the development of coordinated global cooperation in the field of nuclear security, in which the instrument for nuclear security cooperation (insc) plays a key role. building on the framework of nuclear cooperation already developed in the 1990s in central europe and the countries of the former soviet union, this instrument ensures that the eu can act effectively as a global actor in the face of challenges in third countries in the fields of nuclear safety, radiation protection and nuclear safeguards. i am confident that the experience of the european union in this field, both at community level and in the member states (e.g. improved management of radioactive waste), can serve as an example for third countries to adopt similarly high safety standards. i consider it important to extend the standards of transparent risk and safety assessments (resilience testing) to third countries. a common threat assessment system can have a positive impact on the maintenance, regulation and safety of nuclear power plants. this step can also contribute significantly to the development of a nuclear safety culture.
the committee on employment and social affairs has adopted an opinion. − as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on employment and social affairs and as a member of the european parliament's negotiating team, i can say that we have done a great deal of work. and i can express my satisfaction. our expert committee's opinion has been largely incorporated into the text, and will be adopted tomorrow. thank you to the negotiating team for consistently representing the equal opportunity perspective. the legislation is much better in terms of employment, social and equal opportunities than the current rules. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's policy on employment and social inclusion, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's policy on employment and social inclusion. the only thing left to do is to implement the legislation properly, and i would like to draw the commission's attention to that. member states should also fully implement the legislation.
as the labour party's employment coordinator, i welcome the agreement and the current debate, and this european social fund in particular. we who work in social affairs consider it one of the most important eu funds. and i do not agree with the proposals put forward by the mainly communist and green members to suspend the debate, to reopen the debate, to continue. i think the fact of the agreement is a great achievement. we need to have important programmes, whether it's youth initiatives or the poverty funds for the most deprived that are being set up now, to be able to start on 1 january and to be able to move forward in these processes. the crisis is not over, there are now more than 26 million unemployed in the european union. we don't have time for more debate, we have to compromise. and i think that's a good compromise. our colleagues elisabeth morin-chartier and adam kósa have been excellent representatives of the aspects we have jointly defined. i think it is an important achievement, we have already spoken and we have repeated the words about the ambitions of the europe 2020 strategy on poverty, and now we are finally allocating money, the minimum amount of money to be spent, to that 20%. the flexibility elements are important whereby individual countries may raise the age limit for the youth initiative to 30 years if they see fit. and although the member states' call rates are still not 100%, i regard 23.1% as a success, because it is also 1% more than before, and the possibility is open for member states to transfer additional resources to the social fund.
we've had some difficult negotiations, and we're pretty happy with the outcome. as the esf's shadow donor, i would like to thank the commission for its work and, in particular, for the lithuanian presidency's approach to creative negotiations. on the one hand, i have a serious concern about the macroeconomic conditionality that we have heard so much about today, and which is hitting those who need help the most. we can only hope that the built-in conditions will reduce this danger. the other such problem is the proposed esf share in cohesion policy. the difference from the 25% commission proposal is €6.7 billion, and member states are expected to use this money to develop infrastructure that serves short-term political interests rather than improving a disastrous labour market and social situation, rather than reducing poverty. representation of those affected by these problems is rather weak at member state level, whereas investing in human capacity would be in everyone's genuine long-term interest. there are some elements -- i know i have a minute and a half, so i'll go on -- which is an important result. on the one hand, member states need to align their operational programmes with their relevant strategies, such as the roma strategy, the disability strategy, and the provision of quality services and equal access to higher education is also an important element of the agreement. hopefully, the positive elements will work, and we can eliminate the negative ones.
cohesion policy will be a very important tool for the eu member states to kick-start the recovery in some countries and to strengthen it in others, to make job creation programmes successful and to enable more eu citizens to work. i regret that parliament was unable to achieve the deletion of the part concerning the macroeconomic conditionality restricting the use of cohesion funds. this is a concern because it is the result of improper government economic policies that indirectly hurt local governments and private businesses in the very countries where they are most needed. however, it is good that the suspension of payments can only be a last resort and that the 50% ceiling has been accepted. the question of the distribution of regional resources will also be very important, as this will allow us to create jobs in particularly disadvantaged areas, such as hungary, through tourism.
in the air. i am pleased that cohesion policy post-2014 is focusing on results and linking up with the union's new growth strategy, europe 2020. i believe it is important to give sufficient emphasis to flexibility in the member states beyond 2014, as this is the only way to provide tailor-made responses to local and regional challenges. it is regrettable that the macroeconomic conditionality has not been removed from the text of the legislation in the interinstitutional negotiations. the extension of macroeconomic conditionality to items beyond the cohesion fund is fundamentally problematic because it penalizes municipalities, enterprises, individuals for inappropriate economic policy measures by the central government; it sanctions cohesion policy for reasons entirely independent of it; and it does not ensure equal treatment, since different member states benefit from these resources to different degrees. as regards the social fund, i would point out that the esf is by no means the only and exclusive fund which helps to combat unemployment. there are many other factors contributing to the rise in unemployment, such as infrastructure factors, which the european regional development fund is most effective in helping to develop. it is therefore essential to ensure flexibility for member states, as 23.1% is only a minimum value, and member states can spend more on the objectives of the social fund if they consider it necessary.
mr president, parliament is moving this week towards a very important text that could contribute to breaking the glass ceiling which women have been facing for so long. and let us be honest: we have tried self-regulation by the market for a long time and it has failed. women are still very much under-represented in decision making and they continue to face multiple discrimination. without clear and binding legislation, and without the involvement of more women, this is not going to change any time soon. therefore, this is not only about democratic representation; it is also about using all the talent on the labour market. it is not only synonymous with a fairer economy; it is also smart businesses. this is a point on which a majority of european citizens agree, as we have seen from a study prepared by the commission: 75% were in favour. i think that is a very clear signal. and, of course, we finally have the opportunity to bring about some change and to assure equal opportunity to all. the core rapporteurs have done a great job in order to reach a compromise that is both economically sustainable and ambitious. therefore, i would urge you, colleagues, to support this proposal and contribute to another important milestone for the european parliament. i urge you to fight for gender equality and women’s rights.
the rapporteur is the committee on budgetary control. - the details of the compromise on our table have already been discussed by my colleagues in the field. i would like to express my deep and grave indignation at the publication of the draft delegated acts drawn up by the european commission to implement the common agricultural policy, which is to be adopted today. these proposals are clearly contrary to the will of the european council and the european parliament, the european legislators. they severely restrict the content of the common agricultural policy to be adopted today. i believe that if we talk so much about the use of eu funds in the context of the 'naming and shaming' tool, namely the naming of those responsible for the shame, then it is necessary to name the names of those who drew up these draft delegated acts, which are contrary to the intention of the european legislators. i believe that, like the governments of the 23 eu member states, parliament should speak out against this commission proposal and that these delegated acts should be prepared under strict parliamentary scrutiny.
i would like to congratulate commissioner cioloş and all the speakers. the main achievement of the new cap is that it gives member states a much greater margin of manoeuvre than before. hungary's flexibility is enhanced by the fact that, from 2015, the new member states will be able to allocate 13% of their national aid to support sensitive sectors such as livestock, horticulture and viticulture. it is unfortunate that the pig and poultry sectors are still the stepchildren of the common agricultural policy. it is very important that in the coming period, cooperation and integration will become possible not only in the fruit and vegetable sector but also in other sectors. a good compromise was reached on flat-rate support for small farmers, support for young start-up farmers and the aid ceiling. an important result is that it is possible to support small farms below five hectares, which helps hundreds of thousands of hungarian families to survive.
in the air. the negotiations on the new cap were about the survival of the cap. many felt that it was not in their interest to maintain the cap. ferenc gyurcsány, former hungarian socialist prime minister, stated that farmers do not need support. in contrast, the current government has managed to protect farmers' subsidies during the hungarian eu presidency. hungary has achieved a particular success in that we have increased the amount of agricultural subsidies in our country: in the next seven years, hungarian farmers can receive 20% more subsidies than in the previous seven years. we can help hungarian livestock and horticulture with production-related subsidies. it is a unique hungarian success that i propose to increase our country's isoglucose quota by 30 thousand tons. the most effective way to improve the competitiveness of farmers is to reduce energy costs. it is therefore important that 30% of rural development funds should be allocated to investments in renewable energy and energy efficiency improvements. the energy plant will be eligible for direct aid, will be accounted for in the ecological target area and will be able to receive production-related aid. agriculture's most important task is to produce food, as the rapid growth in demand will make food security a priority in the future. no cap measure should endanger food security. greening, i.e. reducing the area under cultivation by 5%, is therefore unacceptable! this could result in a reduction of up to 15 million tonnes of eu cereals production per year and even a net import of cereals.
