in writing. − i would like to welcome this report on the common provisions governing eu funds, which introduces important amendments to the commission’s proposal, in particular for ensuring the contribution of the european structural and investment funds to the unions europe 2020 strategy, arrangements to address the key territorial challenges and to promote the integrated use of the european structural and investment funds. i welcome the explicit reference that special attention should be paid to rural areas and that the implementation of the programme should take into account the overall aim of reducing administrative burden for bodies involved in the management and control of the programmes. it is very important to give local and regional authorities and bodies representing civil society greater rights of participation in planning and implementation and maybe the most significant amendment states that the solutions supported by funds should be integrated, multi-sectoral and multi-dimensional, and it should be possible for the esi funds to be combined into integrated packages that are tailor-made to fit the specific territorial needs. the pre-financing payment is also to be welcomed, which enables member states to provide ex ante support to beneficiaries from the start of the implementation.
in writing. − a large, complex report of almost a thousand pages containing common provisions for the european regional development fund, the european social fund, the cohesion fund, the european agricultural fund for rural development and the european maritime and fisheries fund of the common strategic framework for the period 2014-2020. on behalf of the regional development committee, the text was practically rewritten in its entirety, with the result that its adoption nullifies all other amendments. the regional development committee's values of putting local development, local economy first are close to ours, so i only supported the report by adopting amendment 488. the amendments to the eul/ngl improve social sensitivity, so they are also acceptable to me.
in writing. − i think it is important to maintain the minimum share of the european social fund at 23.1% and not to increase this to 25%. from a procedural point of view, such an attempt would mean the reopening of interinstitutional negotiations, which should not be our aim. we must also bear in mind that the european social fund is by no means the only and exclusive fund to help combat unemployment. there are many factors that contribute to the increase in unemployment, so it is wrong to act on the belief that unemployment can be reduced by simply providing more training. at least as important are the infrastructural factors, to the development of which the european regional development fund contributes most effectively. it is therefore essential to ensure flexibility for member states, as 23.1% is only a minimum value, and member states can spend more on the objectives of the social fund if they consider it necessary.
in writing. − the structural challenges that the eu faces have been compounded by the recent economic and financial crisis, which has resulted in increased levels of unemployment, hitting in particular young people and other vulnerable groups. it is vital therefore to enable the esf to promote sustainable job-creation and support labour mobility, invest in education, skills and life-long learning, promote social inclusion, foster equal opportunities and combat inequality and poverty as well as foster eliminating all forms of discrimination. i hope that the new regulations for the 2014-2020 programming period will make the european social fund more effective in benefiting disadvantaged groups, in particular the long-term unemployed and those systematically excluded from the labour market, such as ethnic minorities, marginalised communities and people facing social exclusion or at the risk of poverty. the sustainable labour market integration of young people, who are not in employment, education or training, is also very important, in particular for young members of marginalised communities, such as young roma. the esf should furthermore provide adequate participation and access for stakeholder non-governmental organisations to actions and the preparation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of programmes, particularly for those ngos that represent or advocate beneficiaries of such programmes.
in writing. − the report sets out guidelines for the european social fund (esf) for the period 2014-2020. the european social fund, established by the treaty of rome in 1957, is the european union's main financial instrument for promoting employment. the commission proposal for the esf has four main objectives: (1) to stimulate employment and labour mobility; (2) to invest in education, skills and lifelong learning; (3) to strengthen social inclusion and the fight against poverty; and (4) to increase institutional capacity and improve the efficiency of public administration. the committee on employment and social affairs has put forward proposals which, in contrast to the original commission document, strengthen the social character of the fund and thus help to concentrate resources on the poorest regions, and i therefore voted in favour of these amendments.
in writing. − i welcome mr olbrycht's report, which calls for better exploitation of the synergies of the horizon 2020 framework programme, better consideration of the needs of regions facing demographic challenges, support for businesses in the field of energy efficiency and renewable energy, and the creation of infrastructure accessible to all.
in writing. − i would like to welcome the initiative to allocate at least 5% of the erdf resources allocated at national level under the investment for growth and jobs goal to integrated actions for sustainable urban development as well as the future establishment of an urban development network to promote capacity-building, networking and exchange of experience at union level between urban authorities responsible for implementing sustainable urban development strategies and innovative actions in the field of sustainable urban development. social and economic developments in urban areas largely influence its surrounding areas and bear proportionally more of the direct or indirect costs of economic productivity, such as congestion, pollution, spatial segregation or criminality. cities are also unevenly affected by social imbalances, such as unemployment, social exclusion and polarisation. it is necessary therefore to assist urban areas in developing their basic physical infrastructure as a precondition for growth and to exploit their potential contribution to economic growth as well as to strengthen the links between urban and rural areas with a view to promoting inclusive development.

in writing. − european territorial cooperation is one of the main pillars of the eu's regional policy and, accordingly, parliament has fought to ensure that this policy area receives funding commensurate with its importance. i am pleased that transnational cooperation also provides support for macro-regional strategies, which are increasingly embracing more regions of the union. the number of authorities involved in enforcement has been reduced and their roles and responsibilities have been clarified.
in writing. − the report deals with the relationship between the european regional development fund (erdf) and european territorial cooperation and identifies what is eligible for erdf resources. these are: cross-border cooperation between associated regions; transnational cooperation covering larger areas involving national, regional and local authorities; cooperation between regions; identification and dissemination of good practice among partners within the union. the erdf should support territorial cooperation, and the fund should contribute to reducing disparities between levels of development, reducing unemployment, promoting information technology and transport links, etc. positive goals, that's why i voted for it.
in writing. − i welcome the fact that the cohesion fund has been extended to support energy efficiency and renewable energy in the housing sector from 2014. in the area of investment priorities, the fund shall pay particular attention to environmental issues. i consider it important that the amounts to be allocated from the cohesion fund to the european network financing facility should not adversely affect the member states most in need of support, which are the main beneficiaries of the cohesion fund.
in writing. − the report is an amendment to the commission's earlier proposal for the cohesion fund. this means, for example, that the aid is directed towards the following objectives: (a) low-carbon economy; (b) adaptation to climate change; (c) protection of the environment and promotion of resource efficiency; (d) sustainable transport; (e) improvement of institutional capacity and efficient public administration. it is an important area for us because the cohesion fund provides support to countries whose per capita gross national income (gni) is less than 90% of the eu27 average. we can access eu funds, so i voted for the report. of course, it would be much better to use the money from our own revenues for what we want, rather than getting a little something back from the eu and labelling it.
in writing. − the draft regulation on the european territorial association contains a number of provisions to promote transparency, simplification and greater efficiency. it is of particular importance that regions and institutions from non-member countries can now become members of the grouping, thus making the egtcs even more effective.
in writing. − the report is an amendment to regulation (ec) no 1082/2006 of the european parliament and of the council on the european grouping of territorial cooperation (egtc). different types of regional associations may be established within the limits of competences under national law in order to overcome obstacles to territorial cooperation. the regulations are acceptable to our country because they provide a framework for international cooperation that hungary can also take advantage of in the carpathian basin, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i consider it a realistic aspiration to increase the participation of women in management positions. we need to create the conditions now to facilitate this. in my view, the problem is a hereditary condition that makes it very difficult for women to reconcile their careers and their private lives. however, there is a great deal of research on this subject which shows that mixed groups perform better and that women's participation has a positive impact on working conditions. quotas may not be the best solution, but i think that the application of quotas now may provide a temporary help in remedying this problem. it is an optimal solution, since it requires a broad social and thought transformation, and this will certainly accelerate this process. in order to catch up with the european union in this area, it is worth following the scandinavian example of taking decisive action, of taking stronger action in the area of regulation.
in writing. the european parliament voted today in plenary on the legislative package on the future of the common agricultural policy. at the start of the reform negotiations, many wanted to abolish the cap and the european system of agricultural subsidies. among them was ferenc gyurcsány, the hungarian socialist prime minister, who declared that farmers did not need support. on the other hand, the hungarian government managed to get a decision to maintain agricultural subsidies during the hungarian presidency of the eu. today's vote has made it clear that the cap has a future. hungary's particular success is that we have not only maintained but even increased the amount of agricultural subsidies in our country: in the next seven years, hungarian farmers can receive 20% more subsidies than in the previous seven years.
in writing. − the revision of the common agricultural policy has produced positive results for hungary, which is why i voted in favour of the interinstitutional agreement. it is an important result for our country that agricultural subsidies will increase by 20% and that the discrimination against hungarian farmers in the new member state will be eliminated in terms of direct payments, so that our producers will receive 100% of the subsidies as well as the producers of the old member states. we also have successfully maintained the most important market regulations. instead of the planned date of 2015, the sugar quota can be maintained until 2017, thus ensuring the operation of the only remaining sugar factory, the plant in kaposi. it is an important step forward that the isoglucose quota of our country can be increased by 30 thousand tons and that the restrictions on vine planting, which protect the less competitive hungarian producers, will remain in force until 2030.
in writing. − the proposal concerns the financing, management and monitoring of the community's agricultural policy (cap). the cap is set to achieve the following objectives: (1) sustainable food production; (2) sustainable management of natural resources and action against climate change; and (3) balanced territorial development. the first pillar of the cap is direct payments and market measures providing basic income support to eu farmers on an annual basis, as well as support in the event of specific market disturbances, and the second pillar is rural development, for which member states draw up and co-finance multiannual programmes under a common framework. although the bureaucracy may increase, our country will receive a significant amount of money, so i voted for the bill. but we must protect our land, we can do it, we just have to want to.
in writing. − this report aims to create the conditions for the provision of correct information on investment products. it was created because it was clear that the banks and investment funds that offered the product were deceiving the public. moreover, retail investors do not have the knowledge and the means to protect their own interests. this is a late and inadequate measure because it would prevent banks from speculating on deposited savings, which would require a separation of commercial and investment banking, as was the case before financial liberalisation. but i had to vote for it because it's still a step forward in protecting the public from the banks.
in writing. − this report is a basic document for rural development stakeholders for the next 7 years and can also be a great reference manual for each issue that arises. the cap rural development pillar is based on six priorities in agriculture, forestry and food processing: 1. promoting knowledge transfer and innovation; 2. increasing competitiveness; 3. promoting food chain organisation and risk management; 4. restoring, preserving and improving the state of ecosystems; 5. promoting resource efficiency and moving towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy; 6. promoting social inclusion, poverty reduction and supporting economic development in rural areas. i voted for it because it's the way to get aid to my country. if you're gonna run in a bag, at least make that bag bigger.
in writing. − the report is designed to regulate the system of area-based direct payments which is vital for our farmers in the present circumstances. the main lines of payments were already set out last year by the ep, the commission and the council. this report is the final state in the sense that the full financial framework was only adopted last week at the eu summit. as the greens and the gue/ngl have also tabled amendments to the position of small producers, i did not support the commission's proposal for a uniform structure. of the two groups' amendments, i voted for the one that gives farmers with less than 5 hectares more of a benefit. it is not the eu's fault that in our country the land and thus most of the subsidies have been in the hands of landowners and foreigners. this is the fault of the governments of all times.

legislative part that it should be a programme country at the time of entry into force of the amending regulation. the council's position reflects that of the commission. however, this approach is (which, i stress, was also considered discriminatory by the council's own legal service), thus reducing the role of parliament to that of an approving body. the intention to speed up the process resulted in a written trialogue, a rapidly convened extraordinary committee meeting and a plenary vote approving the council's position. there would have been no procedural problem if we had agreed on a normal trialogue, voted on the issue at the november committee meeting and brought it before the plenary in december, and the amendment could have entered into force in january. the result is that the original council position was essentially approved by the committee and a discriminatory text was voted by parliament, which contains the possibility of an appeal procedure for breach of equal treatment in relation to the amendment of legislation.

in the air. congratulations to my colleague stolojan on his report, because he did a great job! i have already had the opportunity to speak yesterday in connection with the report on european statistics, about the importance of coordinating and controlling the coordination and control of statistical data and the operation of the national agencies, both at national and european level, in conjunction with the rules laid down jointly. now, in the context of this report, we can be pleased that it is, at the material level, linked to the financial surveillance and economic policy files, and aims at better cooperation between national tax authorities, which includes not only more efficient exchange of information between national tax authorities, but also, for example, joint training of tax officials. in this context, it is welcome that the text has been incorporated, which states that the commission and the member states involved in tax programmes should jointly develop an evaluation system of qualitative and quantitative indicators, on the basis of which the tax programmes can be assessed and evaluated. the report before us, although technical at first glance, is of even greater importance: it concerns some eur 235 million from the next multiannual financial framework, and it is about the fact that the functioning of the internal market can be further strengthened in terms of tax cooperation, and that this report can also contribute to the fight against tax evasion, tax avoidance and double taxation throughout europe! on the basis of all the above, i can only support the report.
the following is the summary of the court of auditors' annual report for 2012:
in writing. − i obviously support this report, as it is a very thorough, detailed and precise piece of material, which has placed european union basic research within the framework of a complete innovation chain from the market (funding) strategy to the market, creating a safety net and a security against the influences that weaken or impede its validation. the report set out in detail all the arguments and reasons which justify the need for such a framework programme in the eu. europe and its citizens are demanding clear answers and adequate security to global challenges, the promotion of the competitiveness of european industries, research on high technology, a stronger emphasis on multidisciplinarity, a broad definition of innovation policies and simplification of the programme. this requirement was met by the report.
in writing. − i believe that security-related research is of fundamental importance to the security and defence sector. these will form an integral part of the horizon 2020 research and innovation framework programmes for the period 2014-2020. as such programmes are the basis for the competitiveness and dynamism of the european defence industry, i support this question with a positive vote.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the implementation of horizon 2020 is a consistent indicator of the direction in which european multi-track innovation can move. this requires a sufficient financial backing for the programme, which can be achieved by allocating eur 100 billion. the commission is also pleased with the professional approach adopted in the section of the proposal which specifically stresses that eu funding for research and innovation should be geared towards a significant increase in private investment, while ensuring that eu funding remains proportionate. i particularly welcome the proposal to set a six-month deadline for industrial players enterprises and highly innovative smes to grant grants, and the related concept of open access and the provision of co-financing.
in writing. − i welcome the commission's proposal for rules on participation and dissemination in horizon 2020 as an important step forward. i think it is important within the programme to define fewer requirements for working time recording and to adopt more widely the accounting practices followed by beneficiaries. however, i would also point out that the programme does not provide for, inter alia, the possibility of recovering indirect costs on the basis of actual costs and that the uniform funding rate does not take into account the specific cost structures of the different participants.
in writing. − the report welcomes the new horizon 2020 regulations as a step forward and the desire to encourage more in-depth consultation with the research and innovation community. the rules should strike a balance between the four key principles of simplification, accountability, flexibility and reliability. from an economic point of view, the financing of activities close to the market should follow a clearly defined concept. union funding for research and innovation should aim to significantly increase private investment. the union funding shall be proportionate and shall not lead to market distortion. the program provides opportunities for domestic universities, institutes and businesses, which is why i voted for the material.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as the eit is a real breakthrough, adding a well-developed educational dimension to the eu's research and innovation policy. although an educational, technological and innovation institution in its own right, the eit should not be seen as a competitor to universities and research centres, but rather as a tool for these institutions to cooperate more effectively, to exchange ideas and experience on a continuous basis and to develop different types of joint projects. i particularly like the proposal for a solution for the location and allocation of resources, which can ensure the legitimacy and independence of the institute, but also its seriousness and its value as such.
in writing. − i see that europe is still not fully out of the crisis, so we need to find ways of developing our capacity for innovation. in the context of horizon 2020, the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) is designed to involve public and private sector as well as academic partners in the innovation process. i'm voting yes on this.
in writing. − the report is about the european institute of innovation and technology (eit). there is agreement that the eit is a key instrument for the union's technology and innovation policy, but certain changes need to be made to better achieve its important objectives. one of these is to strengthen the education sector, to further develop master and doctoral training programmes. two decades ago, we were very good at all of these things, but now our education system is in tatters, our scientists are out of the country, our funding is a disaster. that's why i voted for the report, because it could provide a springboard for the domestic intelligentsia, whom we welcome back and bring back if it's up to us.
in writing. − i welcome the report's commitment to a firm and concrete solution, which will finally bring to fruition the first eu attempt to integrate the three sides of the knowledge triangle (i.e. higher education, research and innovation). the €3 billion budget, supported by the commission and the european parliament, and the reasonably timed release and creation of three new kics are a good way for the eu to pool its efforts to find and implement innovative solutions and to promote entrepreneurship.
in writing. − the european institute of innovation and technology's strategic innovation plan to have the eit's new headquarters in strasbourg. this would immediately attract the attention of the world and europe. and it was seen by european citizens, business and our global partners as an important symbol of the new vision the eu wants to deliver over the next seven years: to focus its attention and commitment on more effective innovation policy. maintaining such a partnership could prove to be of strategic importance from both a technological and economic point of view. such revenues may enable the eit to finance new kics from its budget or contribute to the development of other education projects. that is why i am voting in favour of this question.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a programme to support the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme) (2014-2020). the global competitiveness of european small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) is hampered by market, policy and institutional weaknesses. as a result, european smes are less productive and grow more slowly than their competitors in other parts of the world, and are less able to adapt to change than european large companies. the european union has recognised the importance of smes, and cosme will help them with horizon 2020 instead of the current competitiveness and innovation framework programme (cip).
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european union launching a business development package of over eur 2 billion in the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework as a continuation of previous programmes. the new support programme will boost entrepreneurship, improve the financing environment and increase employment by making it easier and faster to set up a business, facilitating entry into international markets and encouraging young entrepreneurs to set up a business. i consider that national measures are just as important as the eu programme. i consider the hungarian provisions to be exemplary, as in our country the administrative burden on companies and the corporate income tax have been significantly reduced. the hungarian national bank's forint loan programme, which was launched specifically to support small and medium-sized enterprises, has also been a great success.
in writing. − almost three quarters of all jobs in the european union are provided by small and medium enterprises and, furthermore, 85 % of newly established work places between 2002 and 2010 were created by this sector. it can be clearly seen that not only do smes play a key role in the european economy but enhancing their competitiveness and helping them engage more people may also vitally contribute to the recovery from the economic crisis and may reset the eu economy on a trajectory of growth. the union should develop and launch tailor-made programmes in order to boost the entrepreneurial potential of eu citizens, especially targeting vulnerable groups excluded from the labour market, for whom self-employment as an alternative may provide a way out of poverty and marginalisation. in this regard, i would like to welcome the commission’s successfully implemented plan to reduce the administrative burdens by 25 % this year.
in writing. − the current hungarian government only supports domestic enterprises in words, in deeds it favors multi-companies with huge tax breaks, and oppresses small ones with taxes and other means. there are other problems with the global competitiveness of smes, but none of this magnitude. market, policy and institutional weaknesses such as lack of access to finance and markets and regulatory burdens are causing problems. as a result, european smes are less productive and grow more slowly than their competitors in other parts of the world, and they are less able to adapt to change than european large companies. the eu supports businesses through a number of programmes, namely cip, eip and, from 2014, cosme. so, within the framework of eu programmes, opportunities are also opening up for our domestic companies, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − the report could be the self-definition of european research and innovation, as it sets a mirror by acknowledging that europe has lost a lot of its leadership in recent years. it presents europe's 'strengths' and 'weaknesses' in a very definitive and distinctive way, identifying them and providing guidance on how to correct them. in this context, i particularly welcome the proposal in that it sees the solution to so-called 'weaknesses' as, for example, a lack of investment in the knowledge base, or improvements in the lack of framework conditions and bureaucracy, or the effective integration of the contributions of a number of other actors, in addition to parliament's consent. it is precisely this horizontal distinction that makes horizon 2020 more than a simple funding programme that succeeds in achieving a beneficial structural impact on european research organisation.
in writing. − horizon 2020 reinforces europe's leadership in an environment where europe has lost significant ground in recent years. the aim of this programme is to identify europe's strengths and identify the challenges that need to be addressed by mapping out europe's weaknesses. i would like to emphasise in the programme the support for the participation of women and young people in the various projects, and therefore i am voting in favour of this issue.
in writing. − this report is based on a number of parliamentary papers and reports. the proposal represents real progress and is built around four main elements: 1) excellence as one of the driving forces of horizon 2020, 2) building synergies between horizon 2020 and the structural funds, 3) the competitiveness of european industry, 4) issues such as scientific coordination and leadership in each of the thematic areas of horizon 2020. the next horizon 2020 programme will reinforce europe's leadership, but also include identifying and addressing europe's weaknesses. it is certainly a way forward within the present political and economic framework, and i voted in favour of it. of course, for our country, a much better alternative would be to participate in a multi-faceted cooperation
in writing. − the european parliament voted today on the report on european statistics, which focuses on the functioning of the european statistical offices. the document also deals with ensuring professional independence, the availability of resources, guaranteeing strict supervision and applying sanctions in the event of non-compliance with quality standards. i voted in favour of the report because it increases citizens' trust in the eu institutions through stronger eu surveillance and more reliable data.
in writing. − i find this report very welcome and good, as it not only addresses the issue of data collection and service, but also focuses on the functioning of the national statistical offices and provides a framework for creating a culture of accountability across europe. i agree that europe needs a monitoring system that makes statistics quickly and effectively auditable. however, the checks must be justified and must not exceed their scope. they may not therefore interfere with the tasks falling within the competence of the national authority, but may only assist it by giving advice or making recommendations. the report mentions that where a national authority is guilty of providing seriously misleading data, certain sanctions should also be introduced and applied in order to ensure that the quality of statistical reporting is not compromised. i myself agree with this and even suggested in the report, as a separate amendment, that the heads of the national statistical offices should be independent in the performance of their duties and should refrain from incompatible activities, the failure of which will result in immediate suspension and future personal liability. i also think it important to stress that the selection of managers should be on a purely professional basis, free from any politics, and that the recruitment, transfer and dismissal procedures for them should be transparent and also based solely on professional criteria.
in writing. − this programme aiming at the promotion of a high level of quality and sustainable employment, as well as improving working conditions and enhancing the employment and educational situation of young people is responding to maybe the greatest challenge facing the eu. i support the amendment of the title and the consequent extension of the regulation so that it covers social progress as well, which is an unmissable prerequisite for sustainable and inclusive growth. i agree that the programme should explicitly refer to the objectives of the fight against poverty and social exclusion, finding a first job, access to a high level of quality employment, guaranteeing adequate social protection and access to health care for vulnerable people as well as improving working conditions, thereby contributing to social progress. the programme may foster the achievement of these goals through an effective and synergic implementation of all its four axes. the microfinance and social entrepreneurship axis, will hopefully not only help the existing microenterprises and social enterprises, but will also promote access to, and increase the availability of, micro-financing for business start-ups, especially with regard to unemployed, socially excluded and other vulnerable people.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, as it provides for better cooperation between national tax authorities, joint action and, to some extent, joint training of tax officials. in this way, it promotes and integrates with other union policies to avoid tax evasion, tax fraud and double taxation. although the resources of the programme (fiscalis 2020) are limited, i believe that it is worth considering extending the programme to candidate and acceding countries. the fiscalis 2020 programme is highly desirable as it aims to strengthen the internal market by better harmonising and improving the functioning of national tax systems.
in writing. − i consider this report to be of great importance and i have supported it, as it does not depart in any way from the original solvency ii directive, but intends to amend its scope and the date of transposition in order to give member states sufficient time to fully transpose the directive. this new date is amended to 31 december 2014, while maintaining the modern and risk-based system for the full review of european insurance undertakings.

, in writing. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and the survival of marine fish stocks is at risk. as a result, the amount of sea fish caught is steadily and significantly decreasing. the new cfp should pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. hungary has excellent capacity for freshwater fish farming. this not only contributes to food security but also creates a significant number of new jobs. it also increases biodiversity, since the lagoons provide habitat for countless species of birds and other animals. it's no coincidence that most of them are under protection. the new common fisheries policy is giving greater importance to aquaculture, and this trend should continue in the future. the eu budget should provide more financial support to the freshwater aquaculture sector in the 2014-2020 budget period than at present.
rapporteur. − madam president, the poverty and social exclusion that directly affects 80 million europeans is threatening the full range of human rights – not only economic but also social and cultural rights, including the right to an adequate standard of living, the rights to health, housing, food and education, and also civil and political rights. in addition, over the past five years we have been struggling with a long, drawn-out economic crisis with varying degrees of success. the crisis is having a disproportionate impact on the rights of specific groups of people, particularly those who are increasingly vulnerable because they already suffer from discrimination and social exclusion. fear and anxiety caused by the economic downturn have generated a spreading wave of racism and xenophobia which is further weakening the protection of the most vulnerable. first and foremost, it affects the ten million roma in europe who are practically detested in national economies and who sink deeper into poverty. after decades of scrambling from one attempt at economic crisis management to the next under successive governments, it became clear that success called for a solution that we embraced throughout the entire continent and across the political divide. realising that the situation was neither acceptable nor sustainable, the european parliament was a pioneer in demanding an eu-level response to the situation of roma which then became a reality under the hungarian presidency of the eu in the form of an eu framework for national roma inclusion strategies. but the first phase of the framework implementation has already revealed some significant flaws which i address in both my report for the committee on women’s rights and gender equality and in the resolution for the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. i believe that policy-makers should act in five ways to rule out the major risks which we already see: first, national strategies must be brought closer to reality. this would mean that we would have to draw – the commission has to draw – a flowchart of the eu roma inclusion process in order to clarify the state of play as regards implementation and the next steps to be taken as well as to clarify specifically the division of tasks and responsibilities among the stakeholders. at this moment we do not yet know who is responsible for the failure or the success of the roma strategy. it would further imply developing a dashboard of eu roma inclusion indicators adding outcome indicators, baselines, and numerical headline targets to national strategies. this also requires that member states allocate enough financial access to fulfil their policy commitments. in many national action plans this is missing; as is a reflection of the national roma inclusion strategies in their national budgetary policies. you need to know that we found that over the last twenty years, according to studies in several member states, only 10% of the money spent on roma projects has actually reached the roma. second, national strategies must be brought closer to the roma themselves. it means that roma organisations must be strengthened and there needs to be a proper framework consultation, not just platform-based peer learning and the sharing of experiences among policy-makers and roma organisations. also, roma ngos must be strengthened because we need authentic, independent and highly educated roma leaders who actively lead the public discourse on roma and who put community building and social acceptance at the forefront and above the interests of their sponsors. third, national strategies must better target the roma. this means taking into account the multi-dimensional and territorial aspects of poverty and launching integrated, multi-sector development programmes for the most deprived micro-regions by mobilising all available csf funds and other eu instruments because we have learned that the member states have not been using them over the past few years. fourth, national strategies must protect roma; they must go hand-in-hand with the anti-discrimination measures that the commission has already introduced and they have to be much better used. fifth, we also have to bring the balkans into this strategy. from the outset we said that we would like to see the accession countries included in this dossier from the very beginning. what we see is that the successful social and economic inclusion of the roma can only be achieved if we make sure that this risk of failure does arise.
author. − we consider this debate and the decision on roma integration to be important before the end of the parliamentary term. we also welcome the council's proposals, which in many respects emphasize the same things as our proposal. an important outcome of this cycle was the european framework strategy and the fact that each member state produced its own national strategy, but this was more or less the end of the list of positive things. national strategies have largely remained on paper. they do not formulate an action plan, they do not allocate budgetary resources to it, and in fact the use of eu funds is delayed in the member states where they would be most needed for roma integration. segregation in neighborhoods and schools persists, and in many places it is getting worse. there is a lack of political will at national level as well as at local level to promote integration programmes. it is a shame for europe that in the middle of a human rights area millions of people live in third world conditions. when roma leave their homeland, it is not only because of poverty, but also because of the growing anti-gypsyism, discrimination, hate speech and hate crimes. the old member states are no better off. exclusion, illegal expulsion, eviction is a daily occurrence. as european citizens, roma have the same right to free movement as anyone else. if we want to achieve results, we must tackle discrimination, educational and labour market disadvantages in the form of complex programmes, and create adequate housing and access to health services. democratic political parties must clearly distinguish themselves from the exclusionary, hate-mongering manifestations of the far right. the commission should also take clear steps: it should monitor whether member states have actually transposed and applied the racial equality directive, whether they respect the right to free movement and establishment, the right to non-discrimination. if not, you'll have to file a wrongful death suit. member states should seek meaningful dialogue with roma representatives and recognise the importance of roma integration with the non-roma population. they should make the national contact points institutions with real influence. they should ensure that policy decisions do not undermine the objectives of the roma strategy and that operational programmes allocated to eu funds support these objectives. it is also the responsibility of the member states to eliminate institutional discrimination. we know that the situation is bad, but we need accurate data to see where the greatest need for intervention is. data collection and monitoring cannot be left entirely to the member states. there is a need for civil monitoring, so we have proposed building capacity of roma organizations as a pilot project in next year's budget. to be able to act more effectively in the field of roma integration, the eu needs well-educated young roma intellectuals and must support their training through special programmes. it is essential that the commission's directorates-general have roma staff. in preparation for this, there should also be a roma traineeship programme in the commission. in this area, the s&d group is setting an example with its own roma trainee programme. we consider it important that erasmus plus and creative europe programmes also pay particular attention to the inclusion of roma among the beneficiaries. the esf also gives priority to poverty reduction and roma integration. only by taking all these factors into account, by coordinating our efforts and by having a clear political will at national and local level, will we be able to achieve results within a few years.
rapporteur. − mr president, i would like at this stage to thank all those colleagues who have supported my work in parliament in the last nine years; we wanted to manage a complete paradigm shift by making europe understand that inclusion of the roma is very important for europe itself. we wanted to show, through the economic and human rights argument that we presented, that the successful social and economic inclusion of roma, so their figures could approach the regional average, would respond to the demographic challenge of the increasing elderly and decreasing working-age population. this could also trigger substantial economic growth in countries with significant roma populations. i turn to the questions that many people raised – usually those people who like to talk in these debates, to get some votes maybe. those colleagues who have been working on this dossier for a long time however do not just talk about it; they already know that including roma populations in european societies and economies would make sure that this would, in the meantime, mitigate the influx of their migration driven by material interest. so, i would like to highlight once again – also thanking the commission and parliament, and the hungarian presidency as they were the only ones to take this dossier over to the council – that the only answer to many of the questions talked about today is effective inclusion. not inclusion only as window-dressing, not inclusion only on paper, but real effective economic inclusion is the only win-win scenario for europeans and for european citizens who are of roma origin.

the rapporteur. − most eu citizens believe that europe today remains exclusive, with some form of discrimination prevalent. 56% of them believe that discrimination is based on ethnicity, and 46% believe that it is also based on disability or other sexual orientation. the economic crisis has only made it worse. 55% think that inclusive policies have been relegated to the background, especially in the labour market. in contrast, a shocking 37% of people know what their rights are if they are the victim of discrimination. since the treaty of lisbon, the charter of fundamental rights has become legally binding. unfortunately, very few people know what it is and more than two thirds of the population misunderstands its scope. the fact that citizens do not know that the charter is valid only when member states transpose and apply eu law is a source of much frustration and misunderstanding. citizens continue to be uncertain about their rights, how to exercise them and what options they have in the event of violations. more and more citizens are taking advantage of crossborder opportunities and taking up a job or studying in another member state. this, however, requires that they know and be able to exercise their rights under the contracts even in such a situation. yet only 36% feel they know the extra rights that eu citizenship gives them. the fundamental rights agency regularly assesses the situation of the various fundamental rights in the union and highlights a number of shortcomings. anti-semitism, racism, homophobia, xenophobia, intolerance towards others and exclusion are on the rise in the member states, partly as a result of the economic and financial crisis. all of these issues will be addressed by the equality, rights and citizenship programme that we are voting on today. the nearly 440 million euros available over the next seven years will be enough to spend, a paltry sum in view of the scale of the problem. the programme aims to help build a more inclusive society, rejecting exclusion, incitement to hatred and all forms of discrimination. the amount of assigned revenue in accordance with article 21 (3) of the financial regulation is estimated at eur 100000. the community resources available will help to strengthen legal awareness and contribute to the elimination of discrimination, xenophobia and all forms of violence. equality between men and women, the rights of children and persons with disabilities, and the promotion of the additional rights conferred by eu citizenship are given a lot of attention. data protection issues have come to the fore in recent months and are of particular importance in view of the data protection package to be adopted. the council's deliberations lasted almost a year, covering all three presidencies. it was not an easy task, since we had to make sure that compromises were acceptable to everyone, even within parliament. in addition to libe, five other committees submitted opinions to the report. i would like to thank all my colleagues for their work and for the constructive attitude of the commission and the presidencies. the negotiations have enlarged the scope of the objectives. at the in writing. − as a side-effect of globalisation, criminal organisations and terrorist groups have developed cross-border mafia networks, which contribute to the flourishing of activities that threaten human security, such as the illicit accumulation and trafficking of firearms. the situation for law enforcement agencies is further complicated by the fact that, with the advent of the internet, criminals are able to use increasingly sophisticated tools, such as the spread of e-commerce, the online arms trafficking networks. moreover, criminals will always seek to circumvent the strictest rules of the legal market. it is therefore essential to define action at union level and to identify actions that promote the eradication of illicit trade in firearms. strengthening the protocol against the production of and trafficking in firearms is a very important step forward, as it would ensure the protection of citizens, without hampering the legal use of firearms. the protocol supports the development of more effective information exchange, as coordinated cooperation between member states can be one of the most effective methods of dealing with dispersed and organised criminal groups. that is why i support the resolution on the ratification of the protocol.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the proposals contained in it will finally put an end to the biggest problem of the common fisheries policy so far, which is the persistent overfishing. the report says that the council of ministers, when negotiating fishing quotas, should also take decisions that will result in sustainable fisheries. fishermen must take account of the 'maximum sustainable yield', i.e. they must not catch more fish than can be re-produced in a given year. the objective is to maintain the stock above the maximum sustainable yield. in order to put an end to this wasteful practice, which is currently not prohibited, fishing vessels will be obliged to land at least 95% of their catches gradually from 2015. the total catch is determined by area, based on a calendar. i welcome the fact that the european parliament has sought to maintain the highest possible standards in order to achieve a near total ban on the use of shallow drilling. the new marketing rules also guarantee that consumers are better informed, including about the origin of the fish purchased and the fishing techniques used.

in writing. − today, natural and man-made disasters are becoming more frequent, complex and intense, and climate change is expected to lead to more extreme disasters in the future. an important legal instrument for civil protection within the european union is the community civil protection mechanism, which coordinates the preparation and deployment of member states' in-kind assistance (e.g. experts, equipment) in the event of any serious emergency in countries requiring international assistance. the concept of civil protection is interpreted in different ways by the member states, which can be traced back to different historical, political and cultural experiences. although its operational powers are changing over time, i would like to emphasise that the principle of subsidiarity remains in place in relation to civil protection, i.e. it is primarily a matter for the member states. european legislation can therefore only support the actions of the member states and encourage cooperation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the existing eu-wide framework for the management of natural disasters to include the following areas: i also consider it important to establish the emergency response capacity as a voluntary pool of capacities, which is an important factor in creating a more functional european disaster response system. but i would like to stress that military means should only be used as a last resort.

in writing. - foreign exchange loans have made it impossible for tens of thousands of families to live and many have lost their property. i voted in favour of mr presedo's report because it is a proposal that will finally reduce the risk of borrowers: it will regulate the maximum repayment amount, the possibility of changing interest rates, the convertibility of foreign currency loans, and it will introduce reflection time, personalised advice and the requirement of traceability. in my view, the outcome of today's final vote ensures that home buyers across the european union are better informed and better illustrated about the risks of mortgages, the increase in the interest rate due to exchange rate fluctuations and even better protected in the event of a loan default. the stock of private foreign currency loans in hungary is one of the largest, which may have developed because the bankers, instead of warning about the real risks of foreign currency lending, even chased the borrowers into taking irresponsible risks, thus becoming the biggest supporters of the wrong economic policies of the previous governments with this lending practice. meps also want to see the eu's role in the fight against terrorism strengthened, and to ensure that the eu's role in the fight against terrorism is strengthened.

in writing. security and defence policy on the agenda of the european council small steps policy the december european council agenda for the first time since 2008, security and defence policy considerations were also on the agenda. the question of whether the eu can become a self-sustaining, strategically autonomous geo- and defence policy actor on the international stage is again relevant in the run-up to the forthcoming council debate. europe should have an independent defence strategy and an effective security and defence policy which allows for independent action to resolve conflicts, where necessary. a comprehensive eu approach should be developed, taking into account all available tools (old and new) for conflict prevention and crisis management. the revision of the european security strategy, which has been in force since 2003 and was updated in 2008, is also an unavoidable task in the context of changing security threats and in particular the security situation in the eu's neighbourhood. civilian and military capabilities must be adapted to the needs of the future. this may justify the proposal to develop a white paper on security and defence policy, which could also play a role in assessing the capabilities of individual member states coordinating civil and military capabilities. it is welcome that the council meeting has raised these issues to the highest political level, thus contributing to the review of the concept of an autonomous european defence policy. however, given the different economic and political interests of the member states, only small, concrete steps can bring the ideas to be discussed at the council meeting to fruition.

deputising for the rapporteur. − mr president, commissioner, i have taken the place of rafal trzaskowski who has been appointed to a ministerial post in poland. he is co-rapporteur with roberto gualtieri, as you have heard. i think i too can thank the shadows in his name. it is very clear from having read the report that it is a very coherent piece of work. it has fallen to me almost by accident to take on the task of introducing this particular report and i want to add that, given the economic focus of the report, the committee on foreign affairs has worked fairly closely with the committee on economic and monetary affairs and, i think, to good effect. the report is complex and has the objective of assessing the present state of play in the relationship between the different levels of the european union’s institutional framework in economic issues and proposing improvements where these are appropriate. as with any institution – not least one as highly diverse as the eu in all its manifestations – there will be different levels of power and ideally these different levels of power should operate with as much coherence as possible. at the same time, given the european union’s commitment to democracy, it is common sense that there must be clear and transparent procedures in the exercise of power. the report looks specifically at the effectiveness and credibility of economic governance in the context of the euro and various measures taken to establish sustainable remedies for the crisis. the thrust of the report is to develop a strategy in consequence of which economic governance will operate optimally and equally with the necessary democratic legitimacy. roberto gualtieri has already referred to this. similarly, the report has sought to ensure that the coherence of the eu is sustainable at the operational level. now in consequence of the economic crisis of the last few years, the different levels of the eu and member state governance already find themselves intertwined in a variety of ways. the argument of the report is to enhance eu competence where appropriate while respecting fully the demands of member-state-level democracy. this strategy, while essential, is bound to raise complex issues involving all the different levels of governance. one of these levels is the group of states that use the euro and their relationship to the rest of the eu, to the institutions and procedures of the union. the report therefore focuses on the new rules and structures that have been drawn up in the context of the crisis and are understandably euro specific. that does mean that the member states that do not use the euro are excluded from the argument of the report. on the contrary: the relationship between the two tiers affected is part of the discussion. the heart of the report is the need to enhance the eu’s competences in economic policy in strengthening budgetary capacity and the democratic accountability of the commission in these areas. the governance of the emu has to be placed in an overall eu institutional framework as all member states are stakeholders in its governance. as far as the european parliament is concerned, the report stresses that there can be no differentiation been members as far as their country of origin is concerned. however, the internal rules of parliament are flexible enough to establish the most appropriate scrutiny mechanisms. it should be common sense that the area covered by this report is complex and such complexity is bound to generate overlaps and contradictions. to that end, the report has sought to offer lucidity and flexibility in the expectation that its argument offers the most dynamic solution to an issue of paramount importance.
mr. president, colleagues, i have to say that i am very pleased with the results of the vote. i myself consider the report on our table to be a valuable work, but at the same time i have read this document with mixed feelings, mixed feelings arising from a thorough examination of the document as a whole. this report is clearly more than a collection of problems, more than a logical compilation of the questions that need to be answered in order to develop the european union further, but the document that has been produced is, in my opinion, far less than a set of solutions to the pressing problems that affect the european union's everyday life. strengthening the social dimension of economic and monetary union, monitoring the employment aspects of union activities, coordinating member states' employment and social policies more effectively and strengthening social dialogue are important and welcome ambitions. economic policy cannot be managed independently of social policy. the social dimension of the functioning of the union is as important as the economic one. it is important that employment and social considerations are duly taken into account in the formulation and implementation of policies and measures. however, while better coordinating employment and social policies, we must not forget that this is essentially a member state competence and that member states' competences are therefore fully respected. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
mr president, first of all let me congratulate the two co-rapporteurs for this very important and comprehensive report. not only does it provide a deep analysis of the differentiated integration within the european union, taking stock of the changes brought by the necessary strengthening of economic governance at eu level, but it also puts forward concrete solutions in a two-step approach: within the current institutional framework, and what could be done later on through treaty changes. let me emphasise a few key points in this report, concerning the necessary democratic legitimacy, accountability and transparency. this is a crucial requirement of the different measures adopted to strengthen financial stability and economic governance, and although it has often been underlined, for example in the report ‘towards a genuine economic and monetary union’, much improvement is needed and expected. this is especially true of parliamentary scrutiny which is often lacking, for example, with regard to the troika, the efsf, and of course the esm. another point i would like to highlight is the asymmetry that can arise between member states which have the euro as their currency and the other member states which do not. it is important for all member states to remain associated with the mechanism and decisions taken among eurozone members, for the sake of unity and given their implications for the european union as a whole. finally, i welcome the strong emphasis put on the necessary strengthening of the social aspect of the emu and the proposal outlined in the report of expanding the principle of enhanced cooperation to social and employment policies.
deputising for the rapporteur. − mr president, i would like to echo roberto gualtieri. this has been an extremely interesting debate and there are a number of points that i have taken from it. i think the point regarding the complex relationship between unity and differentiation, as raised in the report, is a central one. where the boundary between the two should lie is always difficult to establish and i think the report does offer some clear signposts. the difficulty, of course, lies in the political implications of where we draw that particular boundary. the second point i want to make is that a very strong argument has been made by a number of speakers in this afternoon’s debate in support of social benchmarks, the general social issue to accompany the economic and fiscal ones. i think it is very hard to disagree with this when unemployment is as high as it is in so many states of europe. a third point struck me as being of considerable significance – i think i made it myself at the outset – namely that the democratic legitimacy of whatever we propose is the sine qua non of all development. we have to confront this issue and i think we have to do it effectively. we have to think further about what the most effective mechanisms in this respect actually are. finally, on the issue of treaty change, which has come up several times – various speakers have mentioned it – there has to be considerable support for a move in this direction. many of the changes discussed today necessitate treaty change and i would like to add that a properly organised convention could itself contribute to overcoming the legitimacy deficit.
the next item is the debate on the report by mr alain lamassoure, drawn up on behalf of the committee on constitutional affairs, on relations between the european parliament and the institutions representing national governments (2012/2034 (ini)) (a7-0336/2013).
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, alain lamassoure has produced an extremely cogent and illuminating report. we know that the lisbon treaty has been in effect long enough for us to have valid insights into its workings, and this is what the report has done, notably focusing on one particular area in which the lisbon treaty has left certain points open to interpretation, namely the relationship between the european council and the european parliament. the central proposal of the report is to regulate this relationship in the expectation that the european council will not involve itself in negotiations that are properly handled under the codecision procedure. to this effect, meetings of the european council should be preceded by a debate in parliament with the president of the european council making a presentation in person. then, what the european council actually states should be – it is clear – negotiating instructions for the council of ministers rather than non-negotiable instructions. possibly the most urgent point in the report concerns the election of the president of the commission. respect for the choice of the citizens of europe, as articulated in the elections to the european parliament, is a necessary condition for the legitimacy of the european union as a whole. it is vital that the european council respect this provision. broadly speaking, the underlying thinking behind the report is to strengthen the community method and to dilute the growing trend towards intergovernmentalism in the governance of the european union. in this connection, the role of parliament as a primary body with direct legitimacy is an essential counterweight to intergovernmentalism.
on behalf of the s&d group. – mr president, i would like to thank alain lamassoure for his excellent report. it is always a pleasure to work with him. we have indeed to take stock of the changes that have taken place in practice in recent years, since the adoption of the lisbon treaty. in the light of the crisis in the mechanism aimed at strengthening financial stability and economic governance, and of the legislative work carried on since the beginning of this term, we have witnessed important changes. in particular, the role of the european council and of its president has drastically evolved, sometimes beyond what was foreseen in the treaties. therefore, it is important for this parliament to assess the evolution of the role of the european council and the changing nature of its relationship with the european parliament. working relations between the council and the european parliament should therefore be formalised and enhanced. the evolution of the institutional practices we have witnessed with the crisis calls for much more transparency and democratic accountability. this requires more exchanges with the council, and especially with its president, given the importance his role has taken on. it also requires more open debate and better coordination on both sides, which means getting information sufficiently in advance, which has not always been the case in recent years. taking into consideration the negotiations on the mff, i also believe that the proposal included in the report, to extend the tripartite meetings between the presidents of the institutions beyond budgetary matters, is worth exploring. finally, let me underline how important it is for the european council to clarify how it intends to respect the outcome of the next european elections in appointing the president of the european commission. hopefully, they will be here next time.
